That's why she's so passionate about making sure every child has the same chance to get ahead — in STEM or wherever else they find their calling. = \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Christina Bohannan Date: October 13, 2026 Subject: The engineer = Team, I think my interest in engineering started with my dad. Growing up, I spent a lot of time with him on his construction job sites, where the engineer was the person everyone looked to for answers. I was good at math and science, and with encouragement from my teachers and family, I eventually earned my engineering degree. Looking back, I'm so grateful that I had people in my corner who encouraged me to follow my curiosity. Because for much of history, a girl like me wouldn't have had that opportunity. For centuries, women were routinely excluded from the mathematics and physical sciences. Many weren't given access to formal education, and universities largely shut their doors to women. Womentech Network states that "girls often receive less encouragement to pursue STEM subjects in school" and "are less likely to receive venture capital funding and research grants." Women fought for generations for their rightful place in the STEM fields. On Ada Lovelace Day, I think about trailblazers like Ada Lovelace, Katherine Johnson, Gerty Cori, and Judith A. Resnik, who changed the world. Today, in their honor, we must keep fighting so our girls have every opportunity to succeed. I can't imagine how much brilliance has been overlooked because a girl wasn't encouraged to enjoy math class, couldn't afford college, or was told that engineering wasn't for her. In Congress, I will fight back the best way I know how, by championing funding for public education, strong schools, and an economy with limitless opportunities and enough room to let dreams grow. = Thank you, Christina | Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. **Good Morning!
** **How much money are you throwing away every month without even realizing it?** Your bank. Your cable provider. That subscription you forgot you signed up for. They're all taking a little piece of your paycheck--and those seemingly small charges can add up to hundreds, even thousands, of dollars a year. But some of the biggest money drains aren't hidden fees at all. **They're things millions of Americans keep paying for simply because they've always done it that way.** In this week's [**_Flyover Focus_** ,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyszz9ugzAUgPHT4C3oPWMgDB66ZEulTlEny3-ewa2DI2wHcfuqUY_QA3w_6btd1VWHGNb5Xd9JFp-UT7ZmtdKeI5VCm0IoS1jnfKRqU43O0K5zCeusOPDhhHBC8Vchc9ITceoYSRwnnCbgA7BF8rM3GiaLwo3ak-eT8xo9CtGDGQWwIH81BBTYg8Bz23cEPdd-EKY722FsBJALJW3tVwprWcjHIz1pa226syiXUh656d4afmn45Ui11NZQwy_WqO_b7SN8VsE26R57iDHklzffdYivvvzD-lPynwAAAP__wHRvYg) Ayla counts down [**10 things you should stop paying for**](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyszz9ugzAUgPHT4C3oPWMgDB66ZEulTlEny3-ewa2DI2wHcfuqUY_QA3w_6btd1VWHGNb5Xd9JFp-UT7ZmtdKeI5VCm0IoS1jnfKRqU43O0K5zCeusOPDhhHBC8Vchc9ITceoYSRwnnCbgA7BF8rM3GiaLwo3ak-eT8xo9CtGDGQWwIH81BBTYg8Bz23cEPdd-EKY722FsBJALJW3tVwprWcjHIz1pa226syiXUh656d4afmn45Ui11NZQwy_WqO_b7SN8VsE26R57iDHklzffdYivvvzD-lPynwAAAP__wHRvYg)--and what those expenses could really be costing you. clean_body: From hidden fees to expensive habits, see what's quietly costing you money. | | | Good Morning! How much money are you throwing away every month without even realizing it? Your bank. Your cable provider. That subscription you forgot you signed up for. They're all taking a little piece of your paycheck--and those seemingly small charges can add up to hundreds, even thousands, of dollars a year. But some of the biggest money drains aren't hidden fees at all. They're things millions of Americans keep paying for simply because they've always done it that way. In this week's Ayla counts down what those expenses could really be costing you. This episode is already on pace to become our most-watched Flyover Focus yet, and you won't want to miss it! We're digging into the fuel upgrade drivers spend billions on every year, a bill that can follow families for generations, and everyday charges you may never have thought to question. And the No. 1 item on our list? It's a bill that's still costing millions of American households more than $2,000 a year --and many continue paying it out of pure habit. ➤ How many of these 10 expenses are hiding in your budget? You might be surprised by what's on the list--and how much you could potentially save. () If you enjoy this week's Flyover Focus - there's plenty more where that came from! #### **[Sanford Police Conduct Sweep of International Woolen Mill After Maine Wire Showed it Being Used as a Homeless Encampment](https://substack.com/redirect/1b09f445-e5b8-42bf-859c-6ab3231cc10b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Eighteen officers from Sanford, the State Police, Old Orchard Beach and the York County Sheriff's Office went through the abandoned mill Tuesday morning and found six people inside. Three got trespass summonses. The other three went to jail on warrants and bail violations. Chief Eric Small says Maine law doesn't let him hold anyone for trespass alone, but Sanford officials hope the enforcement action will be one step in the right direction. Tuesday night the council voted to keep Heritage Crossing closed until public safety officials say it's safe.
"I don't police on media reports," Chief Small said, regarding the sweep of the mill building that happened in responser to the Maine Wire's video series showing open drug use and utter despair within the crumbling building.

#### **[EXCLUSIVE: Woman Arrested on Drug OUI After Crashing into Bonny Eagle School Bus](https://substack.com/redirect/24eea044-4357-4c55-8cd3-4058c1aa1642?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
According to the crash report, Annemarie Napolitano, 40, of Westbrook, crossed the centerline on County Road on Friday and hit the cab of a Bonny Eagle school bus with more than a dozen kids aboard. The report says she was looking away from the road, and a blood test allegedly found drugs in her system. Westbrook police put out a press release minutes after our story ran. They also told us she was already out on bail from an August OUI arrest. None of the kids were hurt. Maine Wire reporter Seamus Othot has the [details](https://substack.com/redirect/24eea044-4357-4c55-8cd3-4058c1aa1642?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
#### **[How Candidates for Governor Would Change Maine Health Care Policy](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e005cd-5aa7-438a-b361-9e45dd7772ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Emily Bader's rundown of the three platforms, via [The Maine Monitor](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e005cd-5aa7-438a-b361-9e45dd7772ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Pingree wants a state public option. Bennett wants universal coverage and a medical debt relief fund that starts at $2 million. Charles hasn't published a health plan, but he would fire DHHS leadership and cut the department's budget in half. All three want MaineCare to pay providers more.
#### **[Wanted Harpswell Woman Flees Police and Almost Strikes Deputy Before Causing Crash](https://substack.com/redirect/8f490950-0fe5-4609-b60c-00018cc2ce66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Cumberland deputies say Karen Pennell, 48, pulled over on Harpswell Island Road Monday, then took off when told to get out and nearly hit a deputy. An hour later they found her on Merritt Road and tried to box her in. She got away again, ran a stop sign and hit a pickup. The other driver, 56, had minor injuries. She's charged with driving to endanger, failing to stop and violating release conditions, on top of the original warrant.
#### **[Two LaGrange Felons Arrested After Shooting at Home Across the Street](https://substack.com/redirect/b44b676c-06ad-4c78-93ae-d8668afde23c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Penobscot deputies say two men, 37 and 44, fired across the road last Thursday and hit the house opposite theirs. Both are convicted felons who can't legally own a gun, so that's the charge they got. Nobody has said why they fired. Jail records show both are already out.
## Videos from @TheMaineWire on X
**[Inside Sanford's mill the night before the sweep](https://substack.com/redirect/9ccdad15-244f-4c21-a8c3-e39e7ad49275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**: Monday night, with the police closure supposedly in effect, our crew watched people going in and out of the mill and open-air drug deals nearby. Hours later, 18 officers showed up.
**[Tom Shattuck on Katie Zacharia's first briefing](https://substack.com/redirect/becebb7c-38ee-4e85-bc1f-b508a65fdf6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**: The online left and the legacy press were already going after the new press secretary's first briefing. Tom has some thoughts about that.
## Maine Wire TV
**If you 're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and [Youtube](https://substack.com/redirect/3c3f2ba5-d5e6-4690-bb96-7dbd80af22d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's yesterday's episode...**
**[MWTV - 10/13/26 - Sanford PD Continue Crackdown of Mill](https://substack.com/redirect/0853ffaf-cb3f-440c-a63f-95bbd93c8008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : Tom Shattuck, Graham Pollard, Joe Sokol and Jon Fetherston on the mill crackdown, including Jon's interview with two women at the mill who say police told them to go to Portland. They also cover the Bonny Eagle bus crash, Joe's latest Bangor videos, and the Boston Globe's scrutiny of an independent Massachusetts news site.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0853ffaf-cb3f-440c-a63f-95bbd93c8008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## WVOM Rewind
**[The Maine Wire's Jon Fetherston on WVOM](https://substack.com/redirect/38f19379-e69a-4a25-9ddb-52b81bf20841?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (Monday, about 12 minutes) The feds announced on Friday that they're auditing MaineCare. By Monday morning, Ric Tyler said, the story was already dead at most of Maine's big outlets, so he had Jon on to talk about it. Jon says he's walked The Maine Wire's research into the governor's office more times than he can count. He calls the audit step one of the accountability Dr. Oz told him was coming when Jon showed him around. Jon says the money isn't what bothers him most. It's what he sees in the homes, like staff physically blocking a client from talking to him. He also told Tyler that, in his opinion, people are being told to stand down.
## Politics to Watch this Week...
**Governor 's debate, WMTW**: **tonight, 8 p.m.** Pingree, Charles and Bennett, one hour, moderated by Jon Chrisos. It's their fourth meeting of the general election and their second in two nights. Streams on wmtw.com, WMTW's YouTube and the WABI/WAGM sites.
**Collins vs. Jackson** : On stage Tuesday, Jackson promised to release his first FEC report this morning. As of 7:15 a.m., the FEC still showed nothing from his campaign. The deadline is Thursday. Their final debate is **Thursday, 7 p.m.** at the Gracie Theater in Bangor, the only one with a live audience and voter questions, co-hosted by Maine Public, NEWS CENTER Maine and the Press Herald.
**LePage vs. Dunlap, final 2nd District debate** : also **Thursday, 7 p.m.** , on WABI and WAGM. Two debates at once again, so pick a channel.
**11-day pre-general campaign finance reports** : due **Fri., Oct. 23** from candidates, PACs, ballot question committees and party committees. September lobbying reports are due Thursday.

* * *
# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities and Riyadh airport:** Yemen's Ansarallah [said](https://substack.com/redirect/528bdb8d-a540-4431-842d-e346057402f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday they launched a large-scale attack using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh.
* The group claimed the strikes caused destruction and fires, threatening further attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities in retaliation for Saudi-led attacks in Yemen. Saudi warplanes carried out 104 airstrikes and missile attacks over the past 24 hours across Sana'a, Dhamar, Taiz, Amran, Lahj, al-Jawf, Marib, Saada, and Hodeidah, causing civilian casualties, according to the group.
* Saudi Arabia's military coalition separately [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/aeac9586-4e10-492a-b1a6-824f0376f88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it had intercepted and destroyed an Ansarallah ballistic missile targeting the capital, where authorities issued an air-raid alert urging residents to shelter indoors.
* Four people, including two women, a man, and a child, were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/5822a560-77c9-4725-b75b-39066317622b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Riyadh by falling debris from two intercepted cruise missiles, which also caused minor damage to 15 homes, according to Saudi's Civil Defense. A separate [interception](https://substack.com/redirect/5b6bd717-1a8c-4640-929c-aec0129b7171?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday led to the injury of one person and damage to a house and a vehicle.
* **Saudi Aramco headquarters extensively damaged in Ansarallah attack:** Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran, eastern Saudi Arabia, [suffered](https://substack.com/redirect/f579f715-6098-41d0-b460-72462a0410da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) extensive damage in an attack Tuesday, with a fire spreading across several floors, according to Reuters. The top three floors, where CEO Amin Nasser's office is located, were severely damaged, with collapsed ceilings and shattered windows and doors.
* The fire continued burning into early Wednesday, Reuters reported. Operations at the complex, which houses a control center overseeing oil rigs, refineries, export terminals, and pipelines, have reportedly continued, although some employees were instructed to work from home and certain functions were transferred to global offices. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry described the fire as limited.
* **Saudi-led strikes hit oil facilities in Yemen 's Hodeidah and Sana'a, killing two: **Two people were killed and two others wounded in a Tuesday [airstrike](https://substack.com/redirect/2cd82f36-a446-4d6f-ba5d-e6d882859f9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a state oil company facility in the Ras Isa port area of Hodeidah province, the Sana'a-based Health Ministry said Wednesday. The Saudi-led coalition also struck a Yemeni Oil Company facility in the Ansarallah-controlled capital, Sana'a, after issuing a warning ordering civilians to evacuate the site and nearby storage areas.
* The Yemeni Oil Company claimed its storage facilities were empty and that the strike would not affect fuel reserves or supplies.
* **Yemen hospitals overwhelmed by war casualties as fighting cuts aid to 800,000 people:** Hospitals in Marib, Taiz, and along Yemen's Red Sea coast are [struggling](https://substack.com/redirect/7151ec58-1e5e-4e45-bb39-e45a678ba37d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with unprecedented numbers of war casualties, with some admitting more than 700 wounded patients in a single week, the International Committee of the Red Cross warned Wednesday.
* Fighting and road closures also cut off humanitarian assistance to around 800,000 people in Taiz and other affected areas, according to the UN World Food Programme. Wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, while remaining food supplies in local markets may last only a short time.
* **Cholera cases surge amid mass displacement in unsanitary camps:** Suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in the past three weeks, rising from 217 cases to 647, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/97825ac9-52cd-44dc-ad3f-b43684d67e5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the World Health Organization (WHO). Yemen has reported 8,034 suspected cases of cholera and 27 deaths this year, with a quarter of cases occurring in the last four weeks.
* Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people in the southwest of Yemen--Abyan, Lahj, Al-Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden--accounted for 92% of reported cholera cases.
* "Escalating conflict and mass displacement in Yemen are increasing the risk of infectious disease outbreaks as overcrowding, inadequate access to safe water and disrupted health services expose growing numbers of people to cholera, measles and other preventable diseases," the WHO said.

# Palestine
* **Israeli strike on Gaza City apartment kills Palestinian woman:** A Palestinian woman was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/250da502-4370-4ea2-aab3-7c93efbe4ddf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the Rimal neighborhood, west of Gaza City, early Wednesday, according to WAFA. [Footage](https://substack.com/redirect/34d6094e-763f-401f-90e8-c27748ec831b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) showed a child in shock amid smoke and flames following the strike.
* Over the past 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed--two in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 17 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,392 killed, with 175,440 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,501 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,323, while 838 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli forces uproot olive trees, settlers attack Palestinians across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [uprooted](https://substack.com/redirect/78f5a5f6-79bd-40ab-804c-c678ffe85e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) hundreds of productive olive trees and began leveling farmland in Kafr Malik on Wednesday, WAFA reported.
* Near Deir Dibwan and Burqa, Israeli soldiers assaulted a Palestinian man, confiscated his vehicle, and stole his olive harvest.
* **Nablus:** Israeli settlers attacked farmers harvesting olives in Beita, [beating and injuring](https://substack.com/redirect/c1717155-b0a0-40e7-a0d8-5bd3000ba1b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 17-year-old boy. Settlers also bulldozed land in Beit Dajan to open new roads and around a family home in Burin, reportedly in preparation for a new settlement outpost.
* **Salfit:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/048fe4fa-d1ef-4e6d-b6a4-95ad5a787a43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters in Qarawat Bani Hassan with pepper spray, causing one farmer to suffer breathing difficulties.
* Israeli forces also raided the Palestinian Prisoners Affairs Commission's office in Salfit, damaging its contents, tearing up photographs and interrogating employees.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces [fired tear gas](https://substack.com/redirect/f0732e7d-a833-49ac-b623-691c24c95b7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at olive harvesters from Al-Fandaqumiya, Jaba, and Silat ad-Dhahr, forcing them off their land despite prior coordination allowing access.
* In Ya'bad, settlers assaulted farmers, stole their olive harvest and expelled them from their land, also despite prior coordination.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [kept](https://substack.com/redirect/4a008856-a5d7-4c1f-8ab1-f628d70e16a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) all seven entrances to Tuqu' closed with iron gates for a second consecutive day, blocking other roads with earth mounds and restricting residents' access to work and essential services.
* **Tubas:** Settlers [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/4436b60d-b11c-4baa-bbdb-e95148f15bd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) irrigation networks and agricultural pipelines and stole water valves and meters belonging to farmers in the northern Yarza community.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/2b65db87-1b09-45a3-aa26-b674e90d1301?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eight Palestinians, including four children aged 14 and 15, during raids in Al-Burj, Sa'ir and Beit Ula, reportedly beating several detainees.
* **Over 2,000 Gaza patients die awaiting medical care:** At least 2,027 patients in Gaza have [died](https://substack.com/redirect/b9d49132-ed10-40a7-bd37-3337c60656a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) while awaiting treatment or medical evacuation abroad, while more than 21,000 others need evacuation, according to Mohammed Abu Afash, director of Medical Relief in Gaza.
* Speaking to Voice of Palestine radio on Wednesday, Abu Afash said no patients had left through the Rafah crossing for more than five days, as Israel continues to close crossings and restrict medical supplies.
* Gaza's functioning healthcare centers have fallen from more than 574 to just 227, operating with limited resources, he said.
* **Israeli settlers torch mosque near Jerusalem amid 13 attacks on mosques in 2026:** Dozens of Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/e8ca66c8-cdb2-4aa6-9295-93de6e14644e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the town of Mikhmas, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem, after midnight Wednesday, setting fire to a mosque, burning a Palestinian vehicle and an olive tree, and damaging the mosque's entrance, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission.
* The commission documented 23 incidents of arson or attempted arson targeting Palestinian mosques between January 2023 and October 11, 2026, attributing 20 to Israeli settlers and three to the Israeli military--with 13 incidents so far in 2026, accounting for more than half of all recorded cases.
* Separately, Israeli authorities [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/53890b40-5310-40c4-83cd-382d7bba8584?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 430 homes and structures in occupied East Jerusalem since the start of 2026, with 23,280 demolition orders outstanding and roughly 33% of Palestinian homes at risk.
* **Gaza doctor beaten at prison in front of Israel 's Ben Gvir, Palestinian officials say: **Doctor Marwan Al-Hams, director of Gaza's field hospitals, [suffered](https://substack.com/redirect/3c2537d1-8cc3-493b-aee4-972ad8fb5d5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fractures after being restrained and beaten in front of Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir at Ganot prison on October 7, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and the Prisoners' Media Office.
* The ministry said Al-Hams was restrained, dragged and severely beaten under Ben Gvir's "direct supervision," leaving him with fractures and acute back pain. The Prisoners' Media Office called it the "harshest treatment recorded against Gaza detainees" and said he needs urgent medical care.
* Al-Hams, a Health Ministry spokesperson, was seized by armed men in civilian clothes in Al-Mawasi on July 21, 2025, shot in the leg, and taken. Photojournalist Tamer Al-Za'anin, who was filming him for a documentary, was killed in the attack.

# Iran
* **Three Iranian fishermen seriously injured in drone strike:** Three fishermen were seriously injured Wednesday when a fishing boat was [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/03241222-60e3-4ef9-a225-7937c940f725?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by what local authorities described as an "enemy drone" about 18 nautical miles off Bondaran village in Sirik county, southern Iran, according to Mehr news agency.
* **Iran reports first ship sinking from naval mine in Strait of Hormuz:** A cargo ship carrying approximately 2,500 containers [sank](https://substack.com/redirect/08fd8256-9670-4677-8f33-b18ec677449a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said--marking the first reported sinking of a vessel caused by a mine during the war.
* The IRGC claimed the ship was "carrying contraband" and traveling along "an unauthorized and dangerous route" in the Strait.
* The sinking comes as Tehran reportedly [adopts](https://substack.com/redirect/22e81da3-a20a-44c4-a728-0ba706b42341?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new tactics to increase attacks on vessels it considers in violation of its shipping restrictions, aiming to prevent Washington from lowering oil prices before November's midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters on Wednesday. Shipping attacks have reached their highest intensity since the war began, with 26 vessels hit in the last two weeks.
* Washington has also continued enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports, including a Saturday strike that disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman, according to CENTCOM.
* **Iran carries out latest execution as UN experts call for halt:** Iran executed a man convicted of carrying out a series of shooting attacks in the southern city of Kerman that injured several civilians earlier this year, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB. Ali-Sina Mostafavi was hanged by Iranian authorities on Wednesday.
* Last week, UN experts [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/9d6b2f54-d171-4e8e-b508-8f48e9082653?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iranian authorities to immediately halt all executions, warning that Iran is among a shrinking group of countries that still carries out the death penalty.

# Lebanon
* **Israel strikes multiple towns across southern Lebanon in continued ceasefire violations:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/35b400a3-7c99-486f-8927-4c6439a4ecd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) airstrikes on the outskirts of Hadatha in Bint Jbeil district and between Kfar Tebnit and Nabatieh Al-Fawqa in Nabatieh district on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.
* Israeli forces also shelled the Jallahiya area of Khiam in Marjayoun district, the outskirts of Shaqra and Wadi Al-Salouqi in Bint Jbeil district.
* **UN warns Israeli attacks and destruction in southern Lebanon may amount to war crimes despite ceasefire:** The UN Human Rights Office [expressed](https://substack.com/redirect/d4da2088-be73-4d27-8c24-0c399042b1d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "grave concern" over continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire, citing recent airstrikes, drone attacks, shelling, and explosions across several districts.
* It warned that Israeli forces continue to destroy homes, schools, healthcare facilities, water networks, and farmland in occupied areas of southern Lebanon, leaving entire villages and towns nearly wiped out and preventing thousands of displaced residents from returning.
* The UN said these actions constitute widespread violations of international humanitarian law, some of which may amount to war crimes or other crimes under international law.
* At least 4,387 people, including at least 660 women and children and 135 healthcare workers, were killed between March 2 and October 11, 2026, with another 12,424 injured, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.

# U.S. News
* **Top House Republicans privately concede House control is "all but gone," shift focus to saving Senate majority**: Five senior Republican lawmakers speaking anonymously to Politico [said](https://substack.com/redirect/5b97c2b6-f1ef-4c5f-8f04-a9545770ecc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the House has all but slipped away from the GOP, and that the party's goal is now to limit the scale of the defeat and hold the Senate. One senior House Republican said the aim is to "save as many Republican seats as we can," adding that "President Trump has made this election all about himself. Now we have to survive that political storm." A second lawmaker predicted Democrats would pick up about 10 seats, more than enough for a majority, and said even in newly redistricted Florida and Texas, Republican candidates are "hanging on with their fingernails."
* **Federal probe of Rep. Ilhan Omar reportedly centers on birth date and citizenship papers** : The Department of Justice investigation that led agents to search the Washington residence of **Rep. Ilhan Omar** (D-Minn.) Monday [focuses](https://substack.com/redirect/8518fe34-e226-4b9b-8fb7-e7ba6e9793e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on claims that she or her late father may have lied on decades-old immigration paperwork to secure legal status and eventually citizenship, the Washington Post reported. Omar, whose family fled Somalia and immigrated to the U.S. in 1995, has repeatedly rejected the allegations, calling them "baseless lies and smear campaigns" and the latest attempt by the administration "to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."
* DOJ has filed at least 163 denaturalization cases since January 2025, including 40 since August, versus about 11 a year from 1990 to 2017. Such cases rarely reach decades-old conduct outside serious transnational crimes.
* **DOJ gives California 48 hours to act on alleged noncitizen voter list or face legal action** : In a Tuesday letter to California Secretary of State **Shirley Weber** , [reviewed](https://substack.com/redirect/cb7eb762-fcc6-45f1-a768-fbd748f81c31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Reuters, acting Deputy Attorney **General R. Trent McCotter** demanded the state take a series of actions related to a list of voters until their citizenship is confirmed, including segregating any returned ballots, or face legal action.
* The letter escalates the administration's pressure on states and suggests DOJ may challenge ballots before the Nov. 3 election. DOJ has repeatedly claimed noncitizen voting is widespread despite studies showing it is rare. DOJ's Civil Rights Division has sued 30 states that refused to hand over voter data and has lost 26 cases without a win.
* **NYC Comptroller Mark Levine backs off campaign pledge to buy Israeli bonds:** New York City Comptroller **Mark Levine** said on Wednesday he and his investment team decided not to buy bonds from the state of Israel, the New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/6b12669b-21a8-4d68-8370-f44e8aa3190a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), reversing a campaign promise. He said the call was made "entirely on financial grounds," citing "some technical challenges" and an "ongoing" analysis. Levine, a vocal supporter of Israel, said that, given regional instability and his office's preference for shorter-term bonds, reinvesting made little sense.
* **ICE seeks AI software to monitor detainees ' calls, video and movements**: ICE [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/e3948514-391e-41a4-aa9d-fa5e360fc0b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a request for information Friday on a federal contracting website seeking AI software to use transcription and voice recognition to monitor detainees' calls, along with data from detention-center cameras, the Washington Sun reported on Tuesday. The system would run 24/7 and store detainee profiles.
* ICE already monitors calls not related to detainees' legal cases, but voice recognition would significantly expand its capacity. The software would track whether the person on a call matches the one associated with the dialed number, labeling mismatches "receiver-side deception."
* **Trump pardons two Alaska mechanics on stage at Wasilla rally:** Trump [pardoned](https://substack.com/redirect/e74b730d-ff98-484b-8d4e-baacb124bb1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Alaska mechanics **Zachary Czubak** and **Patrick Fleming** at a Tuesday rally in Wasilla, clearing them of guilty pleas for violating the Clean Air Act. Alaska's congressional Republicans had lobbied for the pardons. Trump called them "unconditional," telling the crowd, "That means you're as clean as a newborn baby's ass," and said they were "worth the eight hours in a plane." Following the live pardons, Czubak urged the crowd to reelect the state's congressional Republicans.
* **CBS analysis: More than half of top bidders for Trump meme coin dinner appear to be overseas** : A CBS News analysis [found](https://substack.com/redirect/81763566-25e8-42b4-abf6-e9f2865d1157?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that at least 52 of the 100 top holders on the public leaderboard for President Trump's next $TRUMP meme coin gala moved funds through crypto exchanges that bar U.S. customers, including Binance, Bybit and MEXC, indicating many are based abroad. At least 44 used Binance before buying.
* The Nov. 22 dinner at Trump National Golf Club outside Washington will seat the 185 largest holders, with Trump as featured speaker alongside three unnamed "legends," and the top 29 get front seating and a VIP reception.
* Trump earned at least $635 million in royalties from the coin last year, part of more than $1.4 billion in crypto-related income, and a Trump Organization affiliate earns revenue whenever it trades.
* **CVS to pay $315 million in unlawful opioids settlement** : CVS Pharmacy and its subsidiaries [agreed](https://substack.com/redirect/8fcb5161-b088-46bf-bad1-e10aa33371e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to pay $315 million to resolve a Justice Department case alleging that it dispensed medically unnecessary prescriptions of highly addictive opioids," the Associated Press reported Tuesday. The suit, filed by the Biden administration's Justice Department in 2024, accused CVS of violating the Controlled Substances Act, filling illegitimate prescriptions for high doses of potent opioids "to fuel its own profits at the expense of public health and safety."
* **Bank of America fined $1.2 billion over customer money laundering** : Bank of America has been fined a near-record $1.2 billion over its failures to monitor and report billions of dollars of suspicious transactions, the Treasury Department and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/282f7658-e76c-4618-b95b-71cd3f14bad3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday.
* The OCC's civil penalty of $750 million, a significant portion of the $1.2 billion total, is the largest it has imposed. The Treasury Department separately announced an $11.6 million sanctions settlement. The Bank of America admitted that it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act, failing to maintain an adequate anti-money-laundering program, conduct due diligence on foreign-correspondent accounts, and file suspicious-activity reports.

# Other International News
* **Ethiopian troops reach Eritrea border, raising war concerns** : Ethiopian government troops on Tuesday [advanced](https://substack.com/redirect/7a659deb-d841-44cd-bff3-54586bb03a20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Zalambessa, a small town bordering Eritrea, Reuters reported. The advance was made against Tigrayan rebels who had controlled the town.
* Ethiopia and Eritrea are on the brink of war, with each lobbing accusations of aggression against the other. Last week, both countries appealed to the UN Security Council for assistance.
* **India orders temporary jailing of two leaders of Cockroach Janta Party** : An Indian court [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/eae8b4c7-2941-4915-90fd-60d769e5838c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the detention of two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, for five days, the party said Wednesday. Alongside about a dozen protesters, they had "scaled barricades" to enter a Delhi observatory that has long been used as an official protest area, Reuters reported, and chanted slogans calling for Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Indian police announced this week that protests would no longer be permitted at the site.
* **Russian strikes kill three people in Kyiv, leave 600,000 without power:** Russian bombardments [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/1fa3eaf4-3cc3-4c91-8de7-434f8f530246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Kyiv and Kharkiv overnight, killing three people in Kyiv and damaging 30 energy facilities, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The strikes caused power outages for at least 600,000 people. Russia's defense ministry said it hit four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. Ukraine reported downing just four of 39 missiles launched on Wednesday.
* **Ukraine hits Russia 's largest data center:** Ukrainian drones struck Russia's largest data center on Wednesday, Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/27daf04e-d97f-469c-8038-ca7a9c6f67f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The firm that owns the data center, Sberbank, is the biggest bank in Russia. Over the last week, Ukraine launched a series of strikes on Russian data centers owned by the technology company Yandex.
* Ukrainian officials [said Wednesday ](https://substack.com/redirect/b60189a0-a80f-4cb7-a27d-968bb53cbf75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)that SpaceX had imposed limits on Starlink services that are used to control combat drones, resulting in the disruption of some missions.
* **Pakistan suspends provincial party of Imran Khan; police assail party supporters** : The Pakistan federal government imposed a state of emergency in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, and placed it under federal control. The move, which federal authorities said was made to combat "[terrorism](https://substack.com/redirect/41c37c08-5363-49ca-a850-757e15d528fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," suspended the provincial rule of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, previously led by Imran Khan, the jailed former prime minister. PTI officials accused the federal government of mounting a coup. Police [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/077797d2-fcea-4622-97d0-7546e1f8562c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas and live rounds at party supporters on Tuesday, according to PTI officials.
* **DRC tops 9,000 Ebola cases, 4,300 deaths:** Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases on Tuesday, the health ministry [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/c27fcb4d-cfe2-49c4-9186-b1058de6780b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The outbreak has killed 4,381 people, and is the largest and deadliest in Congo's history.
* The virus is beginning to spread across borders. Kenya and Uganda have reported Ebola infections originating in Congo.
* **U.S. recalls acting envoy to Nicaragua after Ortega government rejects ambassador nominee** : Acting U.S. envoy to Nicaragua Elias Baumann has [returned](https://substack.com/redirect/9e25ff92-f8a2-42ec-a3e0-ce276e2200c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Washington "for critical consultations," the State Department announced, after Nicaraguan co-Presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo rejected the U.S.'s pick for ambassador, Natasha Franceschi.
* Ortega has accused the U.S. of trying to intervene in Nicaragua's affairs, including institutions like the Organization of American States, which has exerted diplomatic and economic pressure on the Ortega-Murillo government.
* **Russia arrests Japanese journalist, claims "espionage"**: Russia [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/4edf690f-f2b5-4dbf-92f3-5798a139a5ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**** Yuki Imai, a reporter for Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, the federal police agency FSB [said](https://substack.com/redirect/8b2e3f55-ff0e-46f2-bdfb-0658dd07e2cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday. The Russian foreign ministry accused Imai, who was based on the island of Sakhalin, of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory." Imai was arrested by masked agents and flown to Moscow, where a court ordered his detention for two months, the Associated Press reported.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah claims missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities and Riyadh airport: Yemen's Ansarallah Wednesday they launched a large-scale attack using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh. The group claimed the strikes caused destruction and fires, threatening further attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities in retaliation for Saudi-led attacks in Yemen. Saudi warplanes carried out 104 airstrikes and missile attacks over the past 24 hours across Sana'a, Dhamar, Taiz, Amran, Lahj, al-Jawf, Marib, Saada, and Hodeidah, causing civilian casualties, according to the group. Saudi Arabia's military coalition separately it had intercepted and destroyed an Ansarallah ballistic missile targeting the capital, where authorities issued an air-raid alert urging residents to shelter indoors. Four people, including two women, a man, and a child, were in Riyadh by falling debris from two intercepted cruise missiles, which also caused minor damage to 15 homes, according to Saudi's Civil Defense. A separate Wednesday led to the injury of one person and damage to a house and a vehicle. Saudi Aramco headquarters extensively damaged in Ansarallah attack: Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran, eastern Saudi Arabia, extensive damage in an attack Tuesday, with a fire spreading across several floors, according to Reuters. The top three floors, where CEO Amin Nasser's office is located, were severely damaged, with collapsed ceilings and shattered windows and doors. The fire continued burning into early Wednesday, Reuters reported. Operations at the complex, which houses a control center overseeing oil rigs, refineries, export terminals, and pipelines, have reportedly continued, although some employees were instructed to work from home and certain functions were transferred to global offices. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry described the fire as limited. Saudi-led strikes hit oil facilities in Yemen 's Hodeidah and Sana'a, killing two: Two people were killed and two others wounded in a Tuesday on a state oil company facility in the Ras Isa port area of Hodeidah province, the Sana'a-based Health Ministry said Wednesday. The Saudi-led coalition also struck a Yemeni Oil Company facility in the Ansarallah-controlled capital, Sana'a, after issuing a warning ordering civilians to evacuate the site and nearby storage areas. The Yemeni Oil Company claimed its storage facilities were empty and that the strike would not affect fuel reserves or supplies. Yemen hospitals overwhelmed by war casualties as fighting cuts aid to 800,000 people: Hospitals in Marib, Taiz, and along Yemen's Red Sea coast are with unprecedented numbers of war casualties, with some admitting more than 700 wounded patients in a single week, the International Committee of the Red Cross warned Wednesday. Fighting and road closures also cut off humanitarian assistance to around 800,000 people in Taiz and other affected areas, according to the UN World Food Programme. Wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, while remaining food supplies in local markets may last only a short time. Cholera cases surge amid mass displacement in unsanitary camps: Suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in the past three weeks, rising from 217 cases to 647, to the World Health Organization (WHO). Yemen has reported 8,034 suspected cases of cholera and 27 deaths this year, with a quarter of cases occurring in the last four weeks. Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people in the southwest of Yemen--Abyan, Lahj, Al-Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden--accounted for 92% of reported cholera cases. "Escalating conflict and mass displacement in Yemen are increasing the risk of infectious disease outbreaks as overcrowding, inadequate access to safe water and disrupted health services expose growing numbers of people to cholera, measles and other preventable diseases," the WHO said. Palestine Israeli strike on Gaza City apartment kills Palestinian woman: A Palestinian woman was in an Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the Rimal neighborhood, west of Gaza City, early Wednesday, according to WAFA. showed a child in shock amid smoke and flames following the strike. Over the past 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed--two in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 17 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,392 killed, with 175,440 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,501 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,323, while 838 bodies have been recovered. Israeli forces uproot olive trees, settlers attack Palestinians across the occupied West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli forces hundreds of productive olive trees and began leveling farmland in Kafr Malik on Wednesday, WAFA reported. Near Deir Dibwan and Burqa, Israeli soldiers assaulted a Palestinian man, confiscated his vehicle, and stole his olive harvest. Nablus: Israeli settlers attacked farmers harvesting olives in Beita, a 17-year-old boy. Settlers also bulldozed land in Beit Dajan to open new roads and around a family home in Burin, reportedly in preparation for a new settlement outpost. Salfit: Settlers olive harvesters in Qarawat Bani Hassan with pepper spray, causing one farmer to suffer breathing difficulties. Israeli forces also raided the Palestinian Prisoners Affairs Commission's office in Salfit, damaging its contents, tearing up photographs and interrogating employees. Jenin: Israeli forces at olive harvesters from Al-Fandaqumiya, Jaba, and Silat ad-Dhahr, forcing them off their land despite prior coordination allowing access. In Ya'bad, settlers assaulted farmers, stole their olive harvest and expelled them from their land, also despite prior coordination. Bethlehem: Israeli forces all seven entrances to Tuqu' closed with iron gates for a second consecutive day, blocking other roads with earth mounds and restricting residents' access to work and essential services. Tubas: Settlers irrigation networks and agricultural pipelines and stole water valves and meters belonging to farmers in the northern Yarza community. Hebron: Israeli forces eight Palestinians, including four children aged 14 and 15, during raids in Al-Burj, Sa'ir and Beit Ula, reportedly beating several detainees. Over 2,000 Gaza patients die awaiting medical care: At least 2,027 patients in Gaza have while awaiting treatment or medical evacuation abroad, while more than 21,000 others need evacuation, according to Mohammed Abu Afash, director of Medical Relief in Gaza. Speaking to Voice of Palestine radio on Wednesday, Abu Afash said no patients had left through the Rafah crossing for more than five days, as Israel continues to close crossings and restrict medical supplies. Gaza's functioning healthcare centers have fallen from more than 574 to just 227, operating with limited resources, he said. Israeli settlers torch mosque near Jerusalem amid 13 attacks on mosques in 2026: Dozens of Israeli settlers the town of Mikhmas, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem, after midnight Wednesday, setting fire to a mosque, burning a Palestinian vehicle and an olive tree, and damaging the mosque's entrance, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. The commission documented 23 incidents of arson or attempted arson targeting Palestinian mosques between January 2023 and October 11, 2026, attributing 20 to Israeli settlers and three to the Israeli military--with 13 incidents so far in 2026, accounting for more than half of all recorded cases. Separately, Israeli authorities more than 430 homes and structures in occupied East Jerusalem since the start of 2026, with 23,280 demolition orders outstanding and roughly 33% of Palestinian homes at risk. Gaza doctor beaten at prison in front of Israel 's Ben Gvir, Palestinian officials say: Doctor Marwan Al-Hams, director of Gaza's field hospitals, fractures after being restrained and beaten in front of Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir at Ganot prison on October 7, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and the Prisoners' Media Office. The ministry said Al-Hams was restrained, dragged and severely beaten under Ben Gvir's "direct supervision," leaving him with fractures and acute back pain. The Prisoners' Media Office called it the "harshest treatment recorded against Gaza detainees" and said he needs urgent medical care. Al-Hams, a Health Ministry spokesperson, was seized by armed men in civilian clothes in Al-Mawasi on July 21, 2025, shot in the leg, and taken. Photojournalist Tamer Al-Za'anin, who was filming him for a documentary, was killed in the attack. Iran Three Iranian fishermen seriously injured in drone strike: Three fishermen were seriously injured Wednesday when a fishing boat was by what local authorities described as an "enemy drone" about 18 nautical miles off Bondaran village in Sirik county, southern Iran, according to Mehr news agency. Iran reports first ship sinking from naval mine in Strait of Hormuz: A cargo ship carrying approximately 2,500 containers Wednesday after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said--marking the first reported sinking of a vessel caused by a mine during the war. The IRGC claimed the ship was "carrying contraband" and traveling along "an unauthorized and dangerous route" in the Strait. The sinking comes as Tehran reportedly new tactics to increase attacks on vessels it considers in violation of its shipping restrictions, aiming to prevent Washington from lowering oil prices before November's midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters on Wednesday. Shipping attacks have reached their highest intensity since the war began, with 26 vessels hit in the last two weeks. Washington has also continued enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports, including a Saturday strike that disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman, according to CENTCOM. Iran carries out latest execution as UN experts call for halt: Iran executed a man convicted of carrying out a series of shooting attacks in the southern city of Kerman that injured several civilians earlier this year, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB. Ali-Sina Mostafavi was hanged by Iranian authorities on Wednesday. Last week, UN experts Iranian authorities to immediately halt all executions, warning that Iran is among a shrinking group of countries that still carries out the death penalty. Lebanon Israel strikes multiple towns across southern Lebanon in continued ceasefire violations: Israeli warplanes airstrikes on the outskirts of Hadatha in Bint Jbeil district and between Kfar Tebnit and Nabatieh Al-Fawqa in Nabatieh district on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also shelled the Jallahiya area of Khiam in Marjayoun district, the outskirts of Shaqra and Wadi Al-Salouqi in Bint Jbeil district. UN warns Israeli attacks and destruction in southern Lebanon may amount to war crimes despite ceasefire: The UN Human Rights Office "grave concern" over continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire, citing recent airstrikes, drone attacks, shelling, and explosions across several districts. It warned that Israeli forces continue to destroy homes, schools, healthcare facilities, water networks, and farmland in occupied areas of southern Lebanon, leaving entire villages and towns nearly wiped out and preventing thousands of displaced residents from returning. The UN said these actions constitute widespread violations of international humanitarian law, some of which may amount to war crimes or other crimes under international law. At least 4,387 people, including at least 660 women and children and 135 healthcare workers, were killed between March 2 and October 11, 2026, with another 12,424 injured, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. U.S. News Top House Republicans privately concede House control is "all but gone," shift focus to saving Senate majority: Five senior Republican lawmakers speaking anonymously to Politico that the House has all but slipped away from the GOP, and that the party's goal is now to limit the scale of the defeat and hold the Senate. One senior House Republican said the aim is to "save as many Republican seats as we can," adding that "President Trump has made this election all about himself. Now we have to survive that political storm." A second lawmaker predicted Democrats would pick up about 10 seats, more than enough for a majority, and said even in newly redistricted Florida and Texas, Republican candidates are "hanging on with their fingernails." Federal probe of Rep. Ilhan Omar reportedly centers on birth date and citizenship papers : The Department of Justice investigation that led agents to search the Washington residence of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) Monday on claims that she or her late father may have lied on decades-old immigration paperwork to secure legal status and eventually citizenship, the Washington Post reported. Omar, whose family fled Somalia and immigrated to the U.S. in 1995, has repeatedly rejected the allegations, calling them "baseless lies and smear campaigns" and the latest attempt by the administration "to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement." DOJ has filed at least 163 denaturalization cases since January 2025, including 40 since August, versus about 11 a year from 1990 to 2017. Such cases rarely reach decades-old conduct outside serious transnational crimes. DOJ gives California 48 hours to act on alleged noncitizen voter list or face legal action : In a Tuesday letter to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber , by Reuters, acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter demanded the state take a series of actions related to a list of voters until their citizenship is confirmed, including segregating any returned ballots, or face legal action. The letter escalates the administration's pressure on states and suggests DOJ may challenge ballots before the Nov. 3 election. DOJ has repeatedly claimed noncitizen voting is widespread despite studies showing it is rare. DOJ's Civil Rights Division has sued 30 states that refused to hand over voter data and has lost 26 cases without a win. NYC Comptroller Mark Levine backs off campaign pledge to buy Israeli bonds: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine said on Wednesday he and his investment team decided not to buy bonds from the state of Israel, the New York Times , reversing a campaign promise. He said the call was made "entirely on financial grounds," citing "some technical challenges" and an "ongoing" analysis. Levine, a vocal supporter of Israel, said that, given regional instability and his office's preference for shorter-term bonds, reinvesting made little sense. ICE seeks AI software to monitor detainees ' calls, video and movements: ICE a request for information Friday on a federal contracting website seeking AI software to use transcription and voice recognition to monitor detainees' calls, along with data from detention-center cameras, the Washington Sun reported on Tuesday. The system would run 24/7 and store detainee profiles. ICE already monitors calls not related to detainees' legal cases, but voice recognition would significantly expand its capacity. The software would track whether the person on a call matches the one associated with the dialed number, labeling mismatches "receiver-side deception." Trump pardons two Alaska mechanics on stage at Wasilla rally: Trump Alaska mechanics Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming at a Tuesday rally in Wasilla, clearing them of guilty pleas for violating the Clean Air Act. Alaska's congressional Republicans had lobbied for the pardons. Trump called them "unconditional," telling the crowd, "That means you're as clean as a newborn baby's ass," and said they were "worth the eight hours in a plane." Following the live pardons, Czubak urged the crowd to reelect the state's congressional Republicans. CBS analysis: More than half of top bidders for Trump meme coin dinner appear to be overseas : A CBS News analysis that at least 52 of the 100 top holders on the public leaderboard for President Trump's next $TRUMP meme coin gala moved funds through crypto exchanges that bar U.S. customers, including Binance, Bybit and MEXC, indicating many are based abroad. At least 44 used Binance before buying. The Nov. 22 dinner at Trump National Golf Club outside Washington will seat the 185 largest holders, with Trump as featured speaker alongside three unnamed "legends," and the top 29 get front seating and a VIP reception. Trump earned at least $635 million in royalties from the coin last year, part of more than $1.4 billion in crypto-related income, and a Trump Organization affiliate earns revenue whenever it trades. CVS to pay $315 million in unlawful opioids settlement : CVS Pharmacy and its subsidiaries to pay $315 million to resolve a Justice Department case alleging that it dispensed medically unnecessary prescriptions of highly addictive opioids," the Associated Press reported Tuesday. The suit, filed by the Biden administration's Justice Department in 2024, accused CVS of violating the Controlled Substances Act, filling illegitimate prescriptions for high doses of potent opioids "to fuel its own profits at the expense of public health and safety." Bank of America fined $1.2 billion over customer money laundering : Bank of America has been fined a near-record $1.2 billion over its failures to monitor and report billions of dollars of suspicious transactions, the Treasury Department and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Tuesday. The OCC's civil penalty of $750 million, a significant portion of the $1.2 billion total, is the largest it has imposed. The Treasury Department separately announced an $11.6 million sanctions settlement. The Bank of America admitted that it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act, failing to maintain an adequate anti-money-laundering program, conduct due diligence on foreign-correspondent accounts, and file suspicious-activity reports. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ethiopian troops reach Eritrea border, raising war concerns : Ethiopian government troops on Tuesday to Zalambessa, a small town bordering Eritrea, Reuters reported. The advance was made against Tigrayan rebels who had controlled the town. Ethiopia and Eritrea are on the brink of war, with each lobbing accusations of aggression against the other. Last week, both countries appealed to the UN Security Council for assistance. India orders temporary jailing of two leaders of Cockroach Janta Party : An Indian court the detention of two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, for five days, the party said Wednesday. Alongside about a dozen protesters, they had "scaled barricades" to enter a Delhi observatory that has long been used as an official protest area, Reuters reported, and chanted slogans calling for Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Indian police announced this week that protests would no longer be permitted at the site. Russian strikes kill three people in Kyiv, leave 600,000 without power: Russian bombardments Kyiv and Kharkiv overnight, killing three people in Kyiv and damaging 30 energy facilities, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The strikes caused power outages for at least 600,000 people. Russia's defense ministry said it hit four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. Ukraine reported downing just four of 39 missiles launched on Wednesday. Ukraine hits Russia 's largest data center: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's largest data center on Wednesday, Reuters . The firm that owns the data center, Sberbank, is the biggest bank in Russia. Over the last week, Ukraine launched a series of strikes on Russian data centers owned by the technology company Yandex. Ukrainian officials SpaceX had imposed limits on Starlink services that are used to control combat drones, resulting in the disruption of some missions. Pakistan suspends provincial party of Imran Khan; police assail party supporters : The Pakistan federal government imposed a state of emergency in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, and placed it under federal control. The move, which federal authorities said was made to combat "," suspended the provincial rule of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, previously led by Imran Khan, the jailed former prime minister. PTI officials accused the federal government of mounting a coup. Police tear gas and live rounds at party supporters on Tuesday, according to PTI officials. DRC tops 9,000 Ebola cases, 4,300 deaths: Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases on Tuesday, the health ministry . The outbreak has killed 4,381 people, and is the largest and deadliest in Congo's history. The virus is beginning to spread across borders. Kenya and Uganda have reported Ebola infections originating in Congo. U.S. recalls acting envoy to Nicaragua after Ortega government rejects ambassador nominee : Acting U.S. envoy to Nicaragua Elias Baumann has to Washington "for critical consultations," the State Department announced, after Nicaraguan co-Presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo rejected the U.S.'s pick for ambassador, Natasha Franceschi. Ortega has accused the U.S. of trying to intervene in Nicaragua's affairs, including institutions like the Organization of American States, which has exerted diplomatic and economic pressure on the Ortega-Murillo government. Russia arrests Japanese journalist, claims "espionage": Russia ** Yuki Imai, a reporter for Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, the federal police agency FSB Tuesday. **Meg and I voted this morning, and I’m asking you to join us!**

Serving Tennessee in Congress has been the honor of my lifetime. There’s more work to do, and I would be grateful for your vote so I can keep fighting for you and your family in Washington.

**Matt Van Epps** Congressman, TN-07

Massachusetts Republican State Committee Members, RTC Leaders, and Activists,
As Republicans, we all know that a personal message from a friend carries far more weight than a political advertisement.
I hope you will take a few minutes to try Mike Minogue's new Friend-to-Friend Texting program. It is simple: download the Numinar app, match your contacts, and send a personal message to friends and family who may still need a reminder to vote.
Get started here: [https://bradfordwyatt.com/MinogueFriend-To-Friend](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001sDu0BzKgbI_IQlHEDRauXvTX9WBcfIkzTOyhchNr0ezxecgpIsw-8QFhocmuxqKdVn0s0iZ3lOxYSBGmdovgbuDh_bf8vrssuXl1BgSh6mtuC8Y3T7yO1gljcFxqp-3ssZjXlqvQJ_Pf_Dn3KJLyOwGuZIBJ47gbpOTYhnRc80Cpbb4yKp7g4w==&c=eQwSNbxDoyXVAEtfMuTc-V-uZZOeifyHTr2vh254hmZ6TmAAczBuaQ==&ch=KtJ5DB2aHqaNaXiH1Ztfk4jHjdZ13MmHeWPlkv68J3dz9MBXkklSZg==)
The page walks you through every step, including app download, joining the Minogue project, matching contacts, and sending your first text. It also has optional Zoom help sessions if you would like someone to walk through it with you.
After you try it and see how easy it is, please share the page with other activists in your local Republican Town Committee, campaign network, and circle of friends. Friend-to-Friend works best when more people take a few minutes to reach out personally.
Thank you for everything you are doing to help elect Mike Minogue and bring common sense and political balance back to Beacon Hill. Please reach out by email with any questions or concerns [brad@bradfordwyatt.com](mailto:brad@bradfordwyatt.com)

Meg Caldwell didn’t have to die.

She was a bright young woman from Florida. A talented horse rider, the youngest of four sisters. Her family says she was “the light of our lives.”

Sadly, she passed away this year, overdosing on nitrous oxide.

Yet another life lost to drugs. One of more than _200 a day_ in America this year alone.

But what if I told you that Meg’s death, and the epidemic of addiction sweeping the country... has the same root cause as:

* The explosion of pornography and prostitution
* The rise in violent crime and homicide
* The millions of young men addicted to gambling
* And the moral collapse of everyday American life

Because it _does_.

It all stems from [one lie](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=c1b90c156a404224b814fa6155d5e9d7&_e=0BE2ROWaqRGYtjgTWXLxfBQxhKqPY-hblvv6ajEVE7U97e2AMfeZvwntJKagjYwxgqOD7BL4krVxIXuvUbOS3ROduP4vAr-o6B65QaTn5Ln8PcfeLUJgWdp1qlusxoNK-4JX_nMCzIS3hY06hnRAXDo2_AJltMZtvSt6b_A9OGJ8sji_enR5DczWD6O32ALPaGENIphcV9SdBfm4MJdkCXa0rkFImNPwnwPDC10nwmNY_n4v0vQeLb0qScrp_0bSkZz6aUohdTzmmpY-nXYrc01GFo5sQktiBlYs4RGVSBL4efRbBIeIYPuBPS_qRHJmEZr2kT0EN26MtkqGIJBcOmmaHXpTj825r2OcZdDDtdXEziWjyuCQ9W-9Mx59w6NF9Zd7EB-LcvBmE4JAdz8nKO7GwwfUz0AvQMDGMVYvac1kXkaXGCTuX12tPBSIABesPwzFCwSWMhoWI30FJQ7dYcQe4tLYKiiQimBwanV3Q4EJxmiATB_3vw5IR5yvR0LWvqBripPkXjsEQ1hk_egnDslxkY3GUB5NSUiwjVbyWIw%3D).

A lie that has destroyed the fabric of our society...

A lie that has incubated desperation, dependency, and corruption on a tragic scale...

A lie that could be about to spiral into an unstoppable catastrophe, ripping through the lives of hundreds of millions of people.

Last year, we met Donald Trump and his advisors at Mar-a-Lago. They promised this lie would finally be exposed and cast out for good. But they broke that promise. They chose power over truth.

And now _you and your family_ are in the firing line.

So, we’re going public about this lie.

And we’re going to show you how to protect yourself, while there’s still time.

Case File No DRT-ED-PROMISE · Special File · The Broken Promise
Washington Promised to Fix It. Instead, It Now Spends About $3 Billion a Day Just on Interest.
The national debt passed $40 trillion last week. Interest alone now costs more than Medicare. A dollar from 1971 buys about 12 cents’ worth today. Every administration promises to end the problem at its root. None has. Here’s who pays for it.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Every few years, a new team arrives in Washington and promises the same thing: this time, the spending will stop, the debt will come down, and the dollar will be protected. Every few years, the promise quietly expires. The bill doesn’t.
The evidence board
| | What the Numbers Say
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the debt.** On October 8, total U.S. public debt hit a record of about $40.3 trillion, according to Treasury data. Earlier this year, debt held by the public passed the size of the entire U.S. economy for the first time since World War II.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the interest.** Interest on that debt cost $628 billion in just the first seven months of fiscal 2026, more than Medicare, according to the Congressional Budget Office. That works out to roughly $3 billion a day.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — your dollar.** Based on consumer prices, $1 from 1971 has the buying power of about 12 cents today. Prices were still rising 3.4% a year as of August, and gasoline was up 27%.
| OUR THEORY
---
There is one idea underneath all of this: that a government can keep spending money it doesn’t have, and ordinary people won’t pay the price. It’s the most expensive lie in America. Savers pay it through inflation. Young people pay it through homes and futures they can’t afford. And when people stop believing hard work and saving will get them ahead, the damage spreads far beyond the economy.
Decoder
| | The Line That Explains Everything
---|---
| | “The dollar is our currency, but it’s your problem.”— U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally, 1971
---|---
What it says
Washington will manage the dollar to suit Washington.
What it means
**Our theory:** Connally said it to foreign governments. Fifty-five years later, it applies just as well to American families. When the government needs the dollar to be worth less so its debt is easier to carry, the cost falls on everyone holding dollars.
Why it matters to you
| | Where This Hits Home
---|---
| →| **Your savings lose value quietly.** Cash that sits still falls behind every year prices rise.
---|---
| →| **Your taxes go to interest, not services.** Every dollar spent on interest is a dollar not spent on anything you use.
---|---
| →| **Promises won’t protect you.** Every administration has made them. The debt has grown under all of them.
---|---
| ClassificationPromise broken
---
The people in power were told what needs to change, and they chose not to. That leaves families to protect themselves, and the ones who act early have options the others won’t.

They’re now going public with the full story, and with the steps they’re taking to protect their own families.If you have savings, a pension or a family to protect, this is worth seeing while there’s still time.

# **Johnson Unveils Three-Part Plan to Save Nevada’s Millennium Scholarship**
---
| |
### _Proposal restores merit, protects current recipients, and creates permanent funding without raising taxes_
---
| | **Las Vegas, NV —** Nevada State Treasurer candidate Drew Johnson today released a three-part plan to save Nevada’s Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship program. Johnson’s plan reforms future eligibility, protects students already counting on the program, and dedicates a portion of residual unclaimed-property revenue to a permanent scholarship endowment.
The Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship provides eligible Nevada high school graduates up to $10,000 in tuition assistance to attend qualifying Nevada colleges and universities, including the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, the University of Nevada, Reno, and the state’s community colleges.
About $38 million in Millennium Scholarship funds are awarded in a typical year. But the scholarship fund is expected to fall to approximately $21.1 million by the end of FY2027. That insolvency will strip the scholarship from 10,600 current students.
By 2028, the program will be bankrupt, unable to pay for any scholarships because of incompetence and mismanagement by the program’s director and Johnson’s opponent for State Treasurer, Tya Mathis-Coleman.
“The Millennium Scholarship is one of Nevada’s best ideas, but its survival cannot depend on taxpayer bailouts,” Johnson said. “We can honor our promise to current students, restore the scholarship as a meaningful merit award, and build a financial structure that can support it for generations.”
Johnson’s plan to save the Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship program has three parts:
1. **Restore merit.** Beginning with the 2028-29 graduating class, eligibility would generally go to students in the top 20 percent of each qualifying Nevada high school class who complete the required core curriculum and earn at least a 3.0 unweighted core GPA. Scholarship recipients would then need to maintain a 3.0 college GPA to remain eligible.
The plan would include fair, objective alternatives for homeschool students and other students who do not receive a traditional class ranking.

2. **Protect current students and set reasonable limits.** Students who have already qualified would be grandfathered. Future recipients would have four years, rather than six, to use the scholarship, with a limit of eight semesters or 120 credits, while keeping the current $10,000 lifetime cap and reasonable exceptions for military service, disability, and medical hardship.

3. **Build permanent funding.** Nevada would keep the existing tobacco-settlement funding and current $7.6 million annual unclaimed-property transfer. After valid owner claims, program costs, and other statutory obligations are satisfied, 25 percent of the remaining unclaimed-property money that would otherwise automatically be swept into the General Fund would instead support the Millennium Scholarship.

During the transition, that revenue would help stabilize the program, ensuring existing recipients continue to receive their scholarships. Once the program is financially stable, excess revenue would be invested in a permanent Millennium Scholarship endowment, creating an increasingly reliable source of investment income to help fund scholarships for future generations.
The plan would not raise taxes, and all unclaimed property funds would remain fully available for their rightful owners to claim at any time.
Johnson contrasted his proposal with the record and approach of his opponent, Mathis-Coleman.
“Tya Mathis-Coleman has bungled the Millennium Scholarship for 6 years. Her gross mismanagement has left tens of thousands of Nevada’s most promising students wondering if they’ll receive the scholarships they were counting on,” Johnson said. “She has had plenty of time to produce a serious, long-term solution, and we still don’t have one.”
Mathis-Coleman said she would attempt to save the scholarship by asking taxpayers to fund additional bailouts and trying to shake down private businesses to support the scholarship.
“Another taxpayer bailout might keep Millennium alive for a few more years. A few corporate donations might help around the edges. But neither is a mature, responsible solution that fixes the fundamental problem: the scholarship is promising more money than its recurring revenues can sustain,” Johnson said.
“As Treasurer, I will protect the Millennium Scholarship for current students, ensure it is reserved for Nevada’s best and brightest students, and put it on a financial foundation built to last for generations — all without asking Nevada’s already struggling taxpayers to foot the bill.”
Drew Johnson is the Republican nominee for Nevada State Treasurer. He has spent his career in government finance and as a government watchdog exposing waste, fraud, and abuse and fighting to save taxpayers billions of dollars. He intends to continue fighting to protect taxpayers as Nevada’s Treasurer.
For more information about Drew Johnson and his campaign for Nevada State Treasurer, visit [**DrewForNevada.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/ECDsKb3swDu?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d).

Beginning with the 2028-29 graduating class, eligibility would generally go to students in the top 20 percent of each qualifying Nevada high school class who complete the required core curriculum and earn at least a 3.0 unweighted core GPA. Scholarship recipients would then need to maintain a 3.0 college GPA to remain eligible. The plan would include fair, objective alternatives for homeschool students and other students who do not receive a traditional class ranking. 2. Protect current students and set reasonable limits. Students who have already qualified would be grandfathered. Future recipients would have four years, rather than six, to use the scholarship, with a limit of eight semesters or 120 credits, while keeping the current $10,000 lifetime cap and reasonable exceptions for military service, disability, and medical hardship. 3. Build permanent funding. Nevada would keep the existing tobacco-settlement funding and current $7.6 million annual unclaimed-property transfer. After valid owner claims, program costs, and other statutory obligations are satisfied, 25 percent of the remaining unclaimed-property money that would otherwise automatically be swept into the General Fund would instead support the Millennium Scholarship. During the transition, that revenue would help stabilize the program, ensuring existing recipients continue to receive their scholarships. Once the program is financially stable, excess revenue would be invested in a permanent Millennium Scholarship endowment, creating an increasingly reliable source of investment income to help fund scholarships for future generations. The plan would not raise taxes, and all unclaimed property funds would remain fully available for their rightful owners to claim at any time. Johnson contrasted his proposal with the record and approach of his opponent, Mathis-Coleman. “Tya Mathis-Coleman has bungled the Millennium Scholarship for 6 years. Her gross mismanagement has left tens of thousands of Nevada’s most promising students wondering if they’ll receive the scholarships they were counting on,” Johnson said. “She has had plenty of time to produce a serious, long-term solution, and we still don’t have one.” Mathis-Coleman said she would attempt to save the scholarship by asking taxpayers to fund additional bailouts and trying to shake down private businesses to support the scholarship. “Another taxpayer bailout might keep Millennium alive for a few more years. A few corporate donations might help around the edges. But neither is a mature, responsible solution that fixes the fundamental problem: the scholarship is promising more money than its recurring revenues can sustain,” Johnson said. “As Treasurer, I will protect the Millennium Scholarship for current students, ensure it is reserved for Nevada’s best and brightest students, and put it on a financial foundation built to last for generations — all without asking Nevada’s already struggling taxpayers to foot the bill.” Drew Johnson is the Republican nominee for Nevada State Treasurer. He has spent his career in government finance and as a government watchdog exposing waste, fraud, and abuse and fighting to save taxpayers billions of dollars. He intends to continue fighting to protect taxpayers as Nevada’s Treasurer.
