They won't stop until every last race is called ‐‐ so we can't either. Your gift could help do things like secure last‐minute ads to fight back against that GOP propaganda, fund door‐knocking efforts to get out the vote in neighborhoods like yours, print campaign literature explaining the stakes of the race to voters, and even help voters fix rejected ballots so their votes are counted. Your gift now could make the difference between a Democratic victory and another two years of Trump without guardrails. I know that with Trump's inflation hitting us hard, asking for anything is asking for a lot, but I wouldn't ask if it wasn't so important. We need your help to fight for the Senate. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. |

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
subject: Bipartisan bills tackle AI research, kids and chatbots
body:
Plus: new poll finds voters across party lines reject AI safety "hoax" narrative

| | The ARI Briefing * October 2026 | [](https://us.list-manage.com/Tft6T2hVxN3?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---|---
# Congress Takes Up AI Guardrails
Bipartisan bills on chatbots, AI assurance research, and data center transparency
Congress may be in recess for the midterms, but that doesn't mean lawmakers have closed shop for the year. Following a series of whistleblower warnings and AI incidents this summer, members of Congress from both parties have spent the last month putting forward new legislation on some of the most pressing questions in AI policy: how well we understand frontier models adopted for high-risk applications, how chatbots interact with children, and whether communities can see the terms of data center deals before construction begins in their neighborhoods.
ARI endorsed all three bills, each addressing a problem our organization has explored in depth. In today's update, we're sharing more on the latest suite of legislation, new proposals for an AI safety framework, and fresh ARI polling showing that voters across party lines want enforceable federal safety rules for AI.
| | On the Hill | 01
---|---
## Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots
A bipartisan bill would require chatbots to support a non-personified default setting for minors
[](https://us.list-manage.com/JxQy8h0uRqz?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On October 1, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Mike Kennedy (R-UT), Doris Matsui (D-CA), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) introduced the bipartisan [Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act](https://us.list-manage.com/WbVgqpBzEoU?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), which would require developers to design chatbots to support a non-personified setting and make it the default for any user they reasonably know is a minor.
Building on ARI's [non-personified chatbots proposal](https://us.list-manage.com/N5dhNawV0Qr?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), the new bill requires a chatbot to clearly disclose that it is an AI and prevents it from simulating emotional attachment or using manipulative engagement tactics. ARI endorsed the bill as a commonsense measure to protect children, who are especially [vulnerable](https://us.list-manage.com/f5DlME76gJt?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to forming unhealthy relationships with chatbots.
"When kids use an AI chatbot, it should be a tool for learning, not a replacement for friends and family. But to maximize engagement and screen time, chatbots are mimicking human language and connection. A non-personified default setting would make sure that AI doesn't exploit children by pretending to be human and forming relationships."Brad Carson, ARI President
---
In May, ARI [introduced](https://us.list-manage.com/uakekad8aHa?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) the non-personified default setting for chatbots as a necessary safeguard for minors. The proposal recommended the setting require a chatbot to explicitly identify itself as non-human, communicate in a transparent tone, refrain from expressing human emotions and forming relational commitments, and omit language designed to simulate human personality or emotional closeness.
[Read ARI's statement ->](https://us.list-manage.com/vs4s1_L5UCF?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | AI Assurance | 02
---|---
## The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act
Prize challenges would open new pathways to advance AI assurance research
[](https://us.list-manage.com/MOGAMAB2eZw?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
This past summer, a series of rogue AI incidents and whistleblower warnings raised serious questions about AI companies' ability to understand and control advanced AI systems, making it clear that we have not fully developed the technical measures needed to ensure their reliability and safety. Assurance science, the field dedicated to discovering, assessing, and managing AI risks and reliability, is falling short.
Late last month, Reps. August Pfluger (R-TX) and Josh Harder (D-CA) introduced the bipartisan [Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act](https://us.list-manage.com/COp4aEEYGrJ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) (RAIRA) to help close the growing gap between AI development and our understanding of AI systems. The legislation would direct the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to run prize challenges on interpretability and adversarial robustness research, aiming to advance these integral fields while broadening the talent pipeline for AI assurance research, which is critical to proactively identifying misaligned behavior.
As concerns about frontier AI models' capabilities grow, ARI endorsed the bill as a practical step to bolster the security and trustworthiness of AI systems as they are increasingly integrated into high-risk applications.
"Frontier AI companies are building advanced AI models faster than even they themselves can explain how those models think and act. Prize challenges will allow the government to expand the field of AI assurance research so we can understand why models make the decisions they do before an AI crisis devastates our most high-risk systems."Brad Carson, ARI President
---
After the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident, ARI released [an explainer](https://us.list-manage.com/VWMU1y5_nms?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) explaining why labs lack the incentives to fund the assurance research needed to match the pace of AI development, and how the government could fill the gap. Since then, OpenAI and Anthropic have disclosed [additional](https://us.list-manage.com/14T5yd3un4l?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) [incidents](https://us.list-manage.com/lDZvs1yyd3r?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) of misaligned model behavior, increasing the urgency to strengthen the AI assurance field.
[Read ARI's statement ->](https://us.list-manage.com/8D9p5Ie6uy1?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | AI Safety Frameworks | 03
---|---
## Lawmakers Offer New Ideas on AI Safety Frameworks
Two new framework proposals with no mention of state law preemption
This summer's high-profile AI warnings reshaped the world's understanding of AI risks and opened a new window for Congress to develop a federal AI governance framework that meets the moment. In the wake of recent whistleblower warnings, ARI President Brad Carson joined [CNN](https://us.list-manage.com/sTrlhKvtR6s?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), [Fox](https://us.list-manage.com/GkXkMyY7S3p?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), [MS Now](https://us.list-manage.com/1MTnhhippXO?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), and [CNBC](https://us.list-manage.com/hJlBIWIRUgJ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to share a direct message to lawmakers: to address emerging AI risks, we need mandatory, enforceable AI safety standards. Voluntary standards are not enough.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/15cu2zHBzIC?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
In the weeks since those warnings became public, lawmakers have begun work on several AI regulatory frameworks aimed at making that a reality. Earlier this month, Sen. Maria Cantwell, ranking member of the Senate Commerce Committee, published [principles for an AI governance framework](https://us.list-manage.com/vPY5Xjd0mtI?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) designed to keep frontier AI safe. Reps. Sara Jacobs and Don Beyer have announced a [new legislative effort](https://us.list-manage.com/B50UkJJ4SB8?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) on the House side to create an enforceable safety framework with minimum standards and government authority to shut models down if they fail testing requirements. ARI has [applauded](https://us.list-manage.com/17LCnRBZb3D?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) [work](https://us.list-manage.com/8YscNCoW2xY?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) on both of the new proposals.
| | New Polling | 04
---|---
## Voters Don't Buy That AI Safety Is a "Hoax"
Across party lines, Republican and Democratic voters reject the premise
[](https://us.list-manage.com/ZjPeLfgr0Li?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On September 22, ARI [released new polling](https://us.list-manage.com/fzD6lYp0l66?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) showing that Americans are concerned about AI safety and reject the premise that AI risks are a "hoax." Nearly two-thirds of registered voters (62%) say recent incidents involving AI systems expose a real threat, while 23% say concerns about rogue AI agents are a hoax.
That view crosses party lines, with majorities of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans saying recent AI incidents expose a real threat.
| | Real threat | Hoax
---|---|---
Democrats | 67% | 23%
Independents | 63% | 19%
Republicans | 57% | 25%
Concern about losing control of powerful AI is widespread. Nearly four in five registered voters (79%) are concerned that powerful AI systems may act in ways their developers did not intend or cannot control, and more than two-thirds (69%) agree that the federal government should establish binding rules requiring AI companies to ensure their systems are safe and do not harm American families and communities.
[See the full poll ->](https://us.list-manage.com/JKYosMJRudm?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Frontier Oversight | 05
---|---
## From Voluntary Commitments to Binding Standards
Coalitions press the White House and the Senate as AI developers propose independent evaluators
[](https://us.list-manage.com/X3_nf1OFL8X?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On September 9, a broad coalition of 28 public interest and technology policy organizations [sent a letter](https://us.list-manage.com/l5EECcDKEm5?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to the White House urging the release of the Administration's AI framework. The cross-ideological coalition, organized by ARI and the Center for Democracy and Technology, spans groups with differing views on the role of government and technology policy, united around the need for greater transparency and public accountability in how advanced AI systems are evaluated.
Days later, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman [called for](https://us.list-manage.com/11nGDS_tKGc?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) slowing the development of powerful AI models and proposed that their companies give third-party evaluators employee-level access to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments. The move follows calls by ARI for embedded, continuous third-party monitoring of AI development as a core pillar of responsible frontier AI governance. ARI applauded the progress and urged the federal government to make voluntary action enforceable.
On September 16, a coalition of over two dozen AI policy organizations and AI safety leaders [urged the Senate](https://us.list-manage.com/KuJMCkuMotA?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to include clear, binding AI safety standards in any AI regulatory framework.
"We strongly request that any AI regulatory framework empower the government, not AI companies, to set mandatory, binding, and enforceable safety standards for advanced AI. Experience has proven time and again that tech companies cannot be allowed to set their own rules when it comes to the safety of their products."From the coalition letter to the Senate
---
ARI also [urged the Senate to pass](https://us.list-manage.com/JA1mmLp0jTF?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) the bipartisan AI Whistleblower Protection Act, which would extend existing whistleblower protections to shield AI lab employees from retaliation if they disclose significant risks about their work to the American public. ARI endorsed the bill alongside a coalition of tech policy and civil society organizations.
[Read the letter ->](https://us.list-manage.com/EzN_YbecPee?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Data Centers | 06
---|---
## A Strong First Step on Data Centers, and What Comes Next
The House passes a slate of energy bills as a bipartisan bill takes on secret NDAs
[](https://us.list-manage.com/ve7eyYJUdE9?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
In September, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act, and the High-Capacity Grid Act. The bills reflect an important first step towards addressing utility costs for customers, accurate energy forecasting, and grid reliability. ARI [applauded their passage](https://us.list-manage.com/XrU9D5TgieZ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) and called for additional action to address Americans' growing concerns over data centers, including requiring that data centers disclose their electricity usage and putting a stop to the NDAs that keep communities in the dark about how deals are made.
On September 24, Reps. Greg Landsman (OH-01), Tom Barrett (MI-07), and Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced the bipartisan [No Secrets for Data Centers Act](https://us.list-manage.com/12Ey2fUFA4w?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), which would limit the enforceability of NDAs tied to data center construction that involve public officials, land, or incentives. ARI endorsed the legislation, which builds on ARI's [proposal for a Data Center Fair Deal](https://us.list-manage.com/nKpgjfQYf9d?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), as a meaningful move that would empower communities as the data center buildout continues across the country.
"Residents should have a say in whether and how data centers are built in their communities, and transparency will enable them to be a part of these important conversations. This is a critical step toward ensuring that communities can get fair deals before developers break ground."Brad Carson, ARI President
---
According to recent [polling](https://us.list-manage.com/4QEyKfTRyjK?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) by ARI, the vast majority of voters support the disclosure of the terms of data center deals, including tax breaks, electricity arrangements, infrastructure commitments, and other data center incentives.
Watch the panelARI recently hosted [Terms of Service: Community Stewardship in the Data Center Era](https://us.list-manage.com/quYwhbeOnu2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf). The panel, which featured state and local officials from Ohio, Missouri, Georgia, and New York, emphasized the importance of daylighting data center impacts on communities.
---
[Read ARI's statement ->](https://us.list-manage.com/_B71I5mmckf?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | National Security | 07
---|---
## A U.S.-China Channel for AI Incidents
Treasury Secretary Bessent proposes a notification mechanism for AI incidents impacting national security
[](https://us.list-manage.com/13TozU37gd4?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/jN2DqG4lbM2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) that the U.S. has proposed a new notification mechanism for AI incidents impacting national security. The proposal follows calls by ARI for strategic collaboration with China to reduce AI risks and reflects ARI's recommendation for a U.S.-China AI risk reduction channel.
In a [letter to Sec. Bessent](https://us.list-manage.com/RZN8JfgH82I?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), ARI urged the Treasury Secretary to pursue AI talks with China that recognize the security risks posed by AI and to pursue four objectives: a U.S.-China AI risk reduction channel, a reaffirmation of human control over nuclear weapons, a shared AI risk glossary, and regular expert summits on AI risks between the two countries.
"Even in the face of intense competition, the US and China can come to agreement on the need to reduce risks to our national security. It takes political guts to propose collaboration in the face of competitive pressures, and for that, I applaud Sec. Bessent."Brad Carson, ARI President
---
[Read the letter ->](https://us.list-manage.com/QrJzs_0fXeZ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | In the States | 08
---|---
## ARI Launches State-Level AI Advocacy Initiative
New regional teams will support responsible AI policy in the states
[](https://us.list-manage.com/NSWsYHf5e6Z?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
As state legislatures increasingly consider AI policy and regulation, ARI is [launching a dedicated state-level advocacy initiative](https://us.list-manage.com/byFM3NknYZM?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to help lawmakers navigate rapidly evolving AI policy. The new program, supported by a dozen new staff members, will advocate for AI policy in all 50 states. The initiative will address frontier AI risks and threats to workers, children, and families, while offering a public-interest perspective on a wave of industry-backed proposals.
"To succeed in passing the guardrails necessary to sustain AI innovation while protecting the public interest, the state arena can no longer be treated as a secondary front."Brad Carson, ARI President
---
The initiative will give ARI a permanent presence in state capitals across America and will build on the organization's existing federal advocacy, policy expertise, and coalition work. As the team grows, ARI will be hiring for a range of roles across policy, communications, and operations, both in the states and in Washington, with new openings to be announced in the weeks ahead.
[See open roles ->](https://us.list-manage.com/CJwelO9POYN?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| As Congress debates what a federal AI framework should include, we will continue making the case for clear, binding safety standards set by the government, not AI companies.Thank you for being part of ARI's work. Your support enables us to produce cutting-edge research, convene critical conversations, and push for policies that keep emerging technologies aligned with the public interest.Onward,The ARI Team
---

Experience has proven time and again that tech companies cannot be allowed to set their own rules when it comes to the safety of their products."From the coalition letter to the Senate ARI also the bipartisan AI Whistleblower Protection Act, which would extend existing whistleblower protections to shield AI lab employees from retaliation if they disclose significant risks about their work to the American public. ARI endorsed the bill alongside a coalition of tech policy and civil society organizations. | | Data Centers | 06 ---|--- A Strong First Step on Data Centers, and What Comes Next The House passes a slate of energy bills as a bipartisan bill takes on secret NDAs In September, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act, and the High-Capacity Grid Act. The bills reflect an important first step towards addressing utility costs for customers, accurate energy forecasting, and grid reliability. ARI and called for additional action to address Americans' growing concerns over data centers, including requiring that data centers disclose their electricity usage and putting a stop to the NDAs that keep communities in the dark about how deals are made. On September 24, Reps. Greg Landsman (OH-01), Tom Barrett (MI-07), and Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced the bipartisan , which would limit the enforceability of NDAs tied to data center construction that involve public officials, land, or incentives. ARI endorsed the legislation, which builds on ARI's , as a meaningful move that would empower communities as the data center buildout continues across the country. "Residents should have a say in whether and how data centers are built in their communities, and transparency will enable them to be a part of these important conversations. This is a critical step toward ensuring that communities can get fair deals before developers break ground."Brad Carson, ARI President According to recent by ARI, the vast majority of voters support the disclosure of the terms of data center deals, including tax breaks, electricity arrangements, infrastructure commitments, and other data center incentives. On a Tuesday in May, the acting director of ICE stood at a podium and described a labor force that doesn't exist.
Todd Lyons wasn't talking about jobs lost to automation or shipped overseas. He was talking about jobs that never existed at all -- paper jobs, ghost jobs, held by foreign students whose entire right to remain in America depends on those jobs being real. His agency had audited the twenty-five largest employers in the federal government's Optional Practical Training program and identified more than 10,000 foreign students claiming to work for highly suspect employers.
"That's just the tip of the iceberg," Lyons said.
If you've never heard of OPT, that's by design. It is the side door of American immigration. A foreign student on an F-1 visa gets twelve months of work authorization after graduation -- and if the degree is STEM, twenty-four months more. Three years of American employment with no H-1B lottery, no cap, no wage floor, and no requirement that the employer even glance at an American applicant first. By trade-press accounting, roughly half the participants are from India. When Congress declined to expand the H-1B pipeline, OPT quietly grew to fill the gap -- and, it turns out, to industrialize the fraud.
Because when ICE finally started knocking on doors, here is what it found...

bring a new generation of progressive leadership to Congress.

House seat and fight for working families in California’s Central Valley.

⭐ Eli Savit for Michigan Attorney General on the stakes of state-level
races and the importance of electing leaders to hold powerful interests
accountable.

final GOTV sprint.

Hey Peter, John Willoughby here, Kelly’s husband. We’re at the point in the election where it’s all hands on deck, and I wanted to take a moment to tell you about the kind of leader Kelly is – because I think it matters right now more than ever. Kelly and I met during her third year of medical school at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio. **From the very first day I knew her, I watched her pour herself into serving others.** As a resident and as a practicing OB-GYN, she was on call at the hospital at all hours of the day and night, taking care of her patients in their most difficult moments and delivering babies. She passed over 90 bills during her time in the state legislature, fighting for the policies that would make her constituents' lives better. And through it all, she has been an incredible mom to our three kids (and yes, our dog too!). _Kelly has never done anything halfway. She cares deeply, works harder than anyone I know, and fights for what she believes in with everything she has. Kelly is compassionate, and she is tough._ I watched her march right up to armed ICE agents at the Whipple Federal Building and demand to be let in to conduct oversight. I’ve seen her call out this administration’s healthcare misinformation time and time again, using her decades of medical experience to cut through the noise. She was the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill through the Republican-controlled House – and she has passed many more since. She doesn’t just show up. She gets things done._And right now, she needs all of us to show up for her._ Today is Kelly’s last FEC deadline before Election Day. What her campaign raises before the end of the day will shape how strong they go into these final weeks – how many doors get knocked, how many voters get reached, how much ground gets covered.

We’re at the point in the election where it’s all hands on deck, and I wanted to take a moment to tell you about the kind of leader Kelly is – because I think it matters right now more than ever. Kelly and I met during her third year of medical school at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio. From the very first day I knew her, I watched her pour herself into serving others. As a resident and as a practicing OB-GYN, she was on call at the hospital at all hours of the day and night, taking care of her patients in their most difficult moments and delivering babies. She passed over 90 bills during her time in the state legislature, fighting for the policies that would make her constituents' lives better. And through it all, she has been an incredible mom to our three kids (and yes, our dog too!). Kelly has never done anything halfway. She cares deeply, works harder than anyone I know, and fights for what she believes in with everything she has. Kelly is compassionate, and she is tough. I watched her march right up to armed ICE agents at the Whipple Federal Building and demand to be let in to conduct oversight. I’ve seen her call out this administration’s healthcare misinformation time and time again, using her decades of medical experience to cut through the noise. She was the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill through the Republican-controlled House – and she has passed many more since. She doesn’t just show up. What we do in the next few weeks could shape Pennsylvania for years to come. | | | Peter, **This November, the Pennsylvania Working Families Party is backing candidates in _13 races_ where we have a chance to flip a Republican-held seat. ** If we protect our State House majority and flip the State Senate, we could enter 2027 with a Democratic governing trifecta in Harrisburg. That opens the door to a **higher minimum wage** , **paid family** and **medical leave** so caring for someone you love doesn’t mean missing rent, **fully resourced public schools** , **stronger protections for workers** , and **reproductive freedom**. A trifecta won’t deliver those things on its own, but it gives us a new majority to organize alongside and a real path to getting them signed into law. **That’s an opportunity worth going all-in for. clean_body: What we do in the next few weeks could shape Pennsylvania for years to come. | | | Peter, This November, the Pennsylvania Working Families Party is backing candidates in 13 races where we have a chance to flip a Republican-held seat. If we protect our State House majority and flip the State Senate, we could enter 2027 with a Democratic governing trifecta in Harrisburg. That opens the door to a higher minimum wage , paid family and medical leave so caring for someone you love doesn’t mean missing rent, fully resourced public schools , stronger protections for workers , and reproductive freedom. A trifecta won’t deliver those things on its own, but it gives us a new majority to organize alongside and a real path to getting them signed into law. That’s an opportunity worth going all-in for. With just weeks until Election Day, the support we bring in now can help determine how much we’re able to do before voting ends. Against Republicans, we’re backing: Jon Lloyd , State House, District 40 Brad Chambers , State House, District 41 Hadley Haas , State House, District 44 Caleb McCoy , State House, District 79 Sara Agerton , State House, District 88 Fern Leard , State House, District 120 Meriam Sabih , State House, District 131 Rob Gurtcheff , State House, District 170 Thomas Kucer , State House, District 176 Rachel Cuevas , State House, District 187 Mark Pinsley , State Senate, District 16 Chris Thomas , State Senate, District 24 Jackie Baker , State Senate, District 20 See our full list of endorsements . These candidates are talking to voters and making the case for something better. The PA WFP is putting organizing, fundraising support, and resources behind them, and donating today means there’s still time to put your contribution to work: knocking more doors, making more calls, and helping our candidates turn support into votes. Working people deserve a government that takes our needs seriously. This November, we have 13 opportunities to elect people who will help build it. #

Hello there, it’s Scott Kelly. I don’t reach out too often, so when I do, I hope you know it’s important.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261014-2-b&refcode2=11934.3935704.Eu8Ic_&t=1&akid=11934%2E3935704%2EEu8Ic_)_(I'm the one on the left.)_
You might know me as Mark Kelly’s astronaut twin brother. But today, I’m reaching out to you in support of Mark’s wife, my sister-in-law Gabby Giffords’s mission to end gun violence in America.
[**Will you please pitch in $10 to help GIFFORDS PAC reach more undecided voters ahead of the midterms? Early voting is kicking off, and your donations will help us elect gun safety candidates up and down the ballot.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-q42026.p23lnL&refcode=em261014-2-b&t=2&akid=11934%2E3935704%2EEu8Ic_)
**[DONATE NOW](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261014-2-b&t=3&akid=11934%2E3935704%2EEu8Ic_)**
I know Mark and Gabby pretty well, better than most. To know them is to know one thing: **_Don't ever — not even for one moment — underestimate them._**
On January 8, 2011, I was commanding the International Space Station (ISS) when Gabby was shot at a constituent event. It rocked our family forever.
Throughout the next few weeks, I called Mark every day on the phone as he updated me on Gabby’s condition. I traveled to see them immediately after landing.
I am in awe of Gabby. It’s now been fifteen years since that terrible day, but Gabby hasn’t stopped fighting — not only for herself, but for our families across the country.
_But the truth is, not everybody likes that. That’s exactly why the NRA is working so hard to attack Gabby and the incredible work she’s accomplished at GIFFORDS._
It’s never easy watching your family get attacked, but I’m so grateful to know you have their back. Together, you have helped them stand up to the gun lobby and pass more than 820 gun safety laws. That’s no small feat.
**But with the midterms approaching quickly, Gabby can’t finish this fight alone. So I have an important request:**
[**Will you please donate $10 to stand with Gabby today? GIFFORDS PAC is working to take on the gun lobby’s influence in our politics, but Gabby needs your help before her final mid-month deadline of the election >>**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-q42026.p23lnL&refcode=em261014-2-b&t=4&akid=11934%2E3935704%2EEu8Ic_)

---
****
Thank you in advance for supporting Gabby in this fight.
Thank you,
Scott Kelly

**Please, take a second to read this...**
GIFFORDS has been on the front lines to save lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but we can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to stand with Gabby Giffords and donate to GIFFORDS PAC today.**
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/61660?c0=giff-em-q42026.PBv7L4&refcode=em261014-2-b&t=29&akid=11934%2E3935704%2EEu8Ic_)**

Giffords PAC was started to support elected officials who step up to fight the gun violence epidemic. Thank you for standing with Gabby and the Giffords team.

* * *
The wheels are coming off Donald Trump's White House, and the reason is simple: nobody wants to work for him anymore. The last couple of days have been a perfect snapshot of how fractured the MAGA movement has become, and how quickly the people who once begged for a seat at the table are now racing for the exits. But it is the reason they're leaving that tells you everything you need to know about where this presidency is headed.
The rats have been fleeing the Titanic for a while now. An unprecedented number of people have walked out of this White House at a critical moment for the president, heading into a midterm where his party looks like it's going to get creamed and lose the House at minimum, and quite possibly the Senate too. That's why it was so strange to watch Karoline Leavitt bail right in the middle of it. But she sees the writing on the wall. She knows things are about to get ugly, and she doesn't want to spend the next two years of her life on her back foot defending this shit. Because it's one thing to defend Donald Trump when you think you're going to be rewarded for it. It's another thing entirely when you realize you might spend the rest of career answering for it.
So who did they replace her with? Katie Zacharia. And based on her first performance yesterday, she is totally unqualified for the job. She wasn't prepared. She didn't seem to know her stuff. She didn't have the composure. And look, being White House press secretary is an incredibly hard job, even for the best of presidents. You have to step up on day one ready to go, and she clearly wasn't. She confused Trump with her husband. She missed basic facts that were sitting on the sheet right in front of her. She got lost more than once. She looked like a deer in the headlights.
It almost made you feel bad for her, until you remembered she's a crazy right-winger who believes Nazis invented the abortion pill, who has said she doesn't care about the Epstein files, and who has backed ICE agents killing American citizens. It's disgusting stuff. And what's more -- as if that wasn't already enough -- is that before taking this job, Zacharia was a senior communications adviser for Truth Social, Trump's own social media company. The same company that announced it would sell banks and trading firms faster access to Trump's posts, which have literally moved global markets. Think about how insane that is. The lines between the presidency, Trump's business interests, and his propaganda operation have all but disappeared.
And apparently, none of that disqualifies you from standing behind the White House podium. But not knowing what the hell you're doing should.
Then there's Kimberly Guilfoyle. They're forcing her to resign over brazen corruption that, frankly, looks mundane next to what Donald Trump and his family get up to every single day. And now she's out there hinting that she's got some kind of burn book, some stash of compromising material. The administration is reportedly terrified she's going to write a book or talk to the press and badly embarrass her ex-fiance Don Jr., or the president of the United States himself.
That's the part worth sitting with. When your own people stop being assets and start being liabilities, when the folks who know where the bodies are buried start walking out the door with grudges, you've lost control of the operation. The people who were perfectly happy to help him break the government are suddenly a lot less interested in sticking around to answer for it. And it's happening while the economy is failing, the war drags on, and the midterms bear down on them. Every week brings a new scandal, and every scandal makes the next person think twice about signing up.

* * *
It wasn't always like this. Inside the Republican Party, this was the hottest ticket in town. At the beginning, people were lining up to join the Trump administration. They thought it would be a golden age for America, that they were going to build some kind of Republican paradise. They were delusional, of course. You and I knew that. They didn't. Now nobody wants the job, and the best Donald Trump can recruit is the B team, the C team, the D team. I don't even know what letter we're on anymore.
Here's the scary part. We already have unqualified sycophants at multiple layers of our government, from the Pentagon to the military to the FBI to the Food and Drug Administration, people who don't know what they're doing but whose loyalty to Donald Trump is paramount above everything else. Donald Trump spent years making loyalty the only qualification that mattered and he's discovering what happens when that becomes the only thing your people have to offer.
And now even those people are leaving. They're scared of accountability from a Democratic Congress. They can't get done what they came to do. And they can see the president spiraling.
Because he is spiraling. The man is staying up all night posting AI-generated memes of himself wrestling a tiger, just hours after sharing footage of a 23-year-old man being fatally mauled by one. A video the victim's family had pleaded with people to stop circulating.
A tiger.
And somehow, Trump thought the appropriate response to that tragedy was to make himself the star of an AI-generated fantasy about wrestling the animal.
I don't even understand that one. The man needs serious help.
So when you wonder why Donald Trump is handing the White House podium to a second-rate MAGA influencer who was literally working as a communications adviser for the very platform where he's posting this deranged shit, there's your answer. Nobody else will take it. You can laugh and scoff at the absurdity of this administration all you want. God knows I do at times. But there's nothing funny about what happens when the people running your government have absolutely no idea what the fuck they're doing.
Because this isn't just palace drama. When you staff a government with loyalists who can't do the job, the country pays for it. You see it in the economy, where so many people are struggling right now. You see it overseas, where this crew has created a global energy crisis that hurts basically everyone and has pushed more and more of our allies toward our enemies, like China, because they've decided Beijing is a more consistent trading partner than Washington. That's what happens when the D team is running foreign policy.
But the election is three weeks away, and that's an opportunity for the sane wing of this country to get one hand back on the wheel, as imperfect as the Democratic Party can be. It's going to take a couple more years to really right this ship, and you should be prepared for things to get a lot weirder and a lot worse before they get better. But they will get better. This is not sustainable, and the American people understand that in a way they certainly didn't two years ago when they voted this jackass back into office.
Hang in there. Keep doing the work. And take care of yourself.
With urgency,
--Mike

The rats are fleeing the Titanic, and Trump is down to the D team. | | | Oct 14 | | | | | | | | | | | | Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. The wheels are coming off Donald Trump's White House, and the reason is simple: nobody wants to work for him anymore. The last couple of days have been a perfect snapshot of how fractured the MAGA movement has become, and how quickly the people who once begged for a seat at the table are now racing for the exits. But it is the reason they're leaving that tells you everything you need to know about where this presidency is headed. The rats have been fleeing the Titanic for a while now. An unprecedented number of people have walked out of this White House at a critical moment for the president, heading into a midterm where his party looks like it's going to get creamed and lose the House at minimum, and quite possibly the Senate too. That's why it was so strange to watch Karoline Leavitt bail right in the middle of it. But she sees the writing on the wall. She knows things are about to get ugly, and she doesn't want to spend the next two years of her life on her back foot defending this shit. Because it's one thing to defend Donald Trump when you think you're going to be rewarded for it. It's another thing entirely when you realize you might spend the rest of career answering for it. So who did they replace her with? Katie Zacharia. And based on her first performance yesterday, she is totally unqualified for the job. She wasn't prepared. She didn't seem to know her stuff. She didn't have the composure. And look, being White House press secretary is an incredibly hard job, even for the best of presidents. You have to step up on day one ready to go, and she clearly wasn't. She confused Trump with her husband. She missed basic facts that were sitting on the sheet right in front of her. She got lost more than once. She looked like a deer in the headlights. It almost made you feel bad for her, until you remembered she's a crazy right-winger who believes Nazis invented the abortion pill, who has said she doesn't care about the Epstein files, and who has backed ICE agents killing American citizens. It's disgusting stuff. And what's more -- as if that wasn't already enough -- is that before taking this job, Zacharia was a senior communications adviser for Truth Social, Trump's own social media company. The same company that announced it would sell banks and trading firms faster access to Trump's posts, which have literally moved global markets. Think about how insane that is. The lines between the presidency, Trump's business interests, and his propaganda operation have all but disappeared. And apparently, none of that disqualifies you from standing behind the White House podium. But not knowing what the hell you're doing should. Then there's Kimberly Guilfoyle. They're forcing her to resign over brazen corruption that, frankly, looks mundane next to what Donald Trump and his family get up to every single day. And now she's out there hinting that she's got some kind of burn book, some stash of compromising material. The administration is reportedly terrified she's going to write a book or talk to the press and badly embarrass her ex-fiance Don Jr., or the president of the United States himself. That's the part worth sitting with. When your own people stop being assets and start being liabilities, when the folks who know where the bodies are buried start walking out the door with grudges, you've lost control of the operation. The people who were perfectly happy to help him break the government are suddenly a lot less interested in sticking around to answer for it. And it's happening while the economy is failing, the war drags on, and the midterms bear down on them. Every week brings a new scandal, and every scandal makes the next person think twice about signing up. * It wasn't always like this. Inside the Republican Party, this was the hottest ticket in town. At the beginning, people were lining up to join the Trump administration. They thought it would be a golden age for America, that they were going to build some kind of Republican paradise. They were delusional, of course. You and I knew that. They didn't. Now nobody wants the job, and the best Donald Trump can recruit is the B team, the C team, the D team. I don't even know what letter we're on anymore. Here's the scary part. We already have unqualified sycophants at multiple layers of our government, from the Pentagon to the military to the FBI to the Food and Drug Administration, people who don't know what they're doing but whose loyalty to Donald Trump is paramount above everything else. Donald Trump spent years making loyalty the only qualification that mattered and he's discovering what happens when that becomes the only thing your people have to offer. And now even those people are leaving. They're scared of accountability from a Democratic Congress. They can't get done what they came to do. And they can see the president spiraling. Because he is spiraling. The man is staying up all night posting AI-generated memes of himself wrestling a tiger, just hours after sharing footage of a 23-year-old man being fatally mauled by one. A video the victim's family had pleaded with people to stop circulating. A tiger. And somehow, Trump thought the appropriate response to that tragedy was to make himself the star of an AI-generated fantasy about wrestling the animal. I don't even understand that one. The man needs serious help. So when you wonder why Donald Trump is handing the White House podium to a second-rate MAGA influencer who was literally working as a communications adviser for the very platform where he's posting this deranged shit, there's your answer. Nobody else will take it. You can laugh and scoff at the absurdity of this administration all you want. God knows I do at times. But there's nothing funny about what happens when the people running your government have absolutely no idea what the fuck they're doing. Because this isn't just palace drama. When you staff a government with loyalists who can't do the job, the country pays for it. You see it in the economy, where so many people are struggling right now. You see it overseas, where this crew has created a global energy crisis that hurts basically everyone and has pushed more and more of our allies toward our enemies, like China, because they've decided Beijing is a more consistent trading partner than Washington. That's what happens when the D team is running foreign policy. But the election is three weeks away, and that's an opportunity for the sane wing of this country to get one hand back on the wheel, as imperfect as the Democratic Party can be. It's going to take a couple more years to really right this ship, and you should be prepared for things to get a lot weirder and a lot worse before they get better. But they will get better. This is not sustainable, and the American people understand that in a way they certainly didn't two years ago when they voted this jackass back into office. Hang in there. Keep doing the work. And take care of yourself. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. | | | | Friend,
Today, I want to share with you the verse that is at the cornerstone of this campaign.
**_"Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up." - Galatians 6:9_**
My faith in Jesus Christ is what fuels me to keep going every day. It is essential to who I am and everything I do.
The reason I decided to make this verse the foundation of my campaign goes back to 2008. I was in a serious accident that left me with a spinal injury and a long, difficult road to recovery. It took nearly a decade, and I had to relearn how I approached not only my work but my personal life.
I had to figure out how to be there for my family, how to keep showing up for the people I served in the State Senate, and for the clients who trusted me with their financial futures.
During this incredibly tough time, I was reminded of Galatians 6:9. **"****_Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up."_**
My faith and my family kept me going then, and it keeps me going now.
I learned that even when our individual circumstances can be awful, we can respond to the apostle Paul’s teachings and persevere in doing good. Even while I was physically down, I was reminded that I could still serve the people around me. My wife Noel, and my family encouraged me to do what I could to help others, even if it looked a bit different than before.
Now as I run for Governor, that theme of perseverance continues to be especially important.
I’m running for Governor to serve and care for Oklahomans well. I have a plan to cut taxes for seniors and veterans, eliminate the income tax, and bring a turnaround to our education system.
If you want someone in Oklahoma City who knows what it means to keep showing up for the people who depend on him and who by God’s grace won’t stop in the fight to do good, I’m asking for your support.

California has rightfully prided itself on its commitment to helping citizens vote. That's in jeopardy because of a MAGA-led ballot proposal, Proposition 39. Despite President Trump's pushing Prop 39 and its suspect cast of supporters, polling in California shows a close decision.
I get the impulse to oppose fraud--in all its forms. I made my career calling out big banks for mortgage fraud, and then went to Congress where I crusaded against corruption with my whiteboard. Across party lines, we should all fight fraud (wouldn't it be nice if our President and his appointees stopped committing fraud; looking at you, Kimberly Guilfoyle 🙄).
Of course, voting fraud is wrong, and It is a real problem in some democracies in the world. BUT NOT America's and NOT California's. I've seen firsthand in close Congressional elections how carefully ballots are scrutinized to ensure eligibility. The Orange County Registrar of Voters lists the 125 checks that it takes to ensure election integrity: [https://ocvote.gov/security-measures-list](https://substack.com/redirect/5eaa31e3-5d23-4cc3-a399-65eb641ad480?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The office even gives ballot processing tours so Californians can see for themselves exactly how ballots are verified. [https://ocvote.gov/community](https://substack.com/redirect/19244934-70ca-4a03-a1cd-6fc75d878513?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) This is a terrific transparency process that I hope other election officials will offer.
So Proposition 39 is not solving a problem. What it would do it make worse the very real problems created by Trump's lies about voting fraud, especially vote by mail and voting by minorities. Proposition 39 essentially takes Trump's bullshit and would turn it into a terrible amendment to the California constitution.
Look, the proposal sounds straightforward on first glance. Proposition 39 would require voters to either show government-issued ID every time they vote in person at the polls or to put part of their Social Security numbers on the outside of their ballot envelopes by mail. The problem is reality, which is where many seemingly innocuous government policies end up creating harms. Not every U.S. citizen has a government identification that matches their current name and address (heck, given my son's initial efforts at learning to drive, I thought he might not have a license by this November. He does; buckle up out there!). Four in 10 voters ages 18-24 do not have a driver's license. One in five people with disabilities do not have a drivers license. Other voters have divorced or married and not yet changed their IDs, have moved frequently with multiple addresses, or have another small discrepancy. (One of my voting-age kids has a middle name that is spelled differently on his social security card and his passport because my ex-husband had sloppy handwriting in the hospital room; ask me how long this has been on my to-do list to try to fix.)
It's just not true that as long as you are a U.S. citizen and eligible to vote, you'll be fine on Election Day. If Proposition 39 were to become law, a citizen's rightful eligibility to vote could be preempted by a recently expired ID, a forgotten wallet (these kids just use ApplePay on their phones!), a middle initial mismatch, unclear rules about what government IDs count (does a public school ID card work?), and faulty "non-citizen" databases for verification that we know are rife with errors.
Enforcing such rules would inevitably produce long lines and uneven enforcement. Already California sometimes sees lines that stretch for hours; I've seen this firsthand in every election in the last decade at UC Irvine. Turning voters away isn't just about partisanship; sometimes it's about an election volunteer who decides to overzealously --and unlawfully -- enforce rules. As a poll watcher in a deep blue pocket of Massachusetts, I personally saw election officials invent reasons to deny voters like "you cannot bring a stroller in here" and "I cannot find your name"--without asking for the spelling to even try.
Finally, as a lifelong consumer advocate, I cannot overstate the risks of requiring voters to put the last four digits of their social security numbers on the OUTSIDE of their ballots. With those four-digits, a home address, and an internet connection, identity theft is easy peasy. Seniors who are warned repeatedly by the Social Security Administration to never disclose their social security number to a stranger would simply omit the digits, and have their mail-in ballots tossed.
Our democracy today has real challenges: big money in politics, relatively low voting rates, rampant gerrymandering, and more. The election security risks that America faces do not come from individuals voting who are not eligible. The real election security risks are from foreign interference or hacking--and even election-denying Republicans, as I saw firsthand in the Capitol on January 6th, 2021.
Proposition 39 isn't about election integrity. It's yet another play by Trump to make voting harder, sow distrust about our democracy, and create chaos. Don't let Trump corrupt California's elections. Vote NO on Prop 39.

Hey y’all,
My opponent stood on a stage next to Donald Trump in Clarksville this past weekend and told Tennesseans to be patient about high prices.
Be patient. That’s the message he had for families filling up at the pump and checking out at the grocery store, for farmers watching tariffs and an expensive war eat into everything they’ve worked for.
That’s nonsense. Tennesseans are working hard and still coming up short, and nobody in this district has been sitting around waiting for a politician to tell them to wait. They deserve a representative who takes high prices seriously, not one who shares a stage with the people driving them up and asks you to hang in there.
I’m running for Congress to lower costs and give working families some breathing room. I oppose the tariffs. I oppose the war in Iran. That’s the job we’re interviewing for.

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: At What Point Do We Say Enough?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/10lcfw3i3tc?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/H8YQeEADDno?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends,There is a question I keep coming back to as I look at the direction of Johnson County:**At what point do we say enough is enough?** In 2021, Johnson County had a budget of approximately **$1.24 billion.** Today, it is **$1.9 billion.** That is an increase of roughly **52% in five years.** Can we continue down a path where government spending grows at such an unchecked pace?Consider the new Johnson County Health Services Building. The project now carries a price tag of approximately **$116.5 million for 140,000 square feet** , or about **$832 per square foot.** For perspective, 2025 RSMeans construction data puts even a Kansas City-area **hospital at approximately $523 per square foot at the 75th percentile.** Different buildings have different requirements, and no construction benchmark is a perfect comparison. But a difference of more than **$300 per square foot** should at least cause us to ask questions.**What are we getting for the additional cost? What alternatives were considered? Where was the pressure to find a better value for taxpayers?** And Mike Kelly’s answer...”we are constructing a building in line with costs of other recent government projects”. WOW, thanks for pointing out the waste in all levels of government. Of course, that gets to the larger issue.**I believe the job of the County Commission is not simply to hear what staff wants and approve it.**
* It is to ask questions.
* To challenge assumptions.
* To demand measurable results.
* To distinguish between what would be nice to have and what taxpayers truly need.
* And, sometimes, to say **no**.

Good leadership is not about cutting services simply for the sake of cutting. It is about making sure every dollar has a purpose and that taxpayers are receiving value for what they spend.**So I will ask the question again: At what point do we say enough is enough and demand change?** Here is how you can help!Every $25, $50, $100, or $250 contribution helps us reach another voter, put another sign in the ground, boost another digital ad and make the case for a different direction in Johnson County.[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/QhNdfwx0cGe?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) And money alone will not win this election.We are in the final stages of this race, and volunteers are more important than ever. Knock doors. Make calls. Put up signs. Talk to your neighbors.[**JOIN THE TEAM**](https://us.list-manage.com/cNEViINUOft?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) I promise to fight to bring about positive change and fiscal sanity. **Are you ready to join me?**
Karen Crnkovich

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Friends,There is a question I keep coming back to as I look at the direction of Johnson County:At what point do we say enough is enough? In 2021, Johnson County had a budget of approximately $1.24 billion. Today, it is $1.9 billion. That is an increase of roughly 52% in five years. Can we continue down a path where government spending grows at such an unchecked pace?Consider the new Johnson County Health Services Building. The project now carries a price tag of approximately $116.5 million for 140,000 square feet , or about $832 per square foot. For perspective, 2025 RSMeans construction data puts even a Kansas City-area hospital at approximately $523 per square foot at the 75th percentile. Different buildings have different requirements, and no construction benchmark is a perfect comparison. But a difference of more than $300 per square foot should at least cause us to ask questions.What are we getting for the additional cost? What alternatives were considered? Where was the pressure to find a better value for taxpayers? And Mike Kelly’s answer...”we are constructing a building in line with costs of other recent government projects”. WOW, thanks for pointing out the waste in all levels of government. Of course, that gets to the larger issue.I believe the job of the County Commission is not simply to hear what staff wants and approve it. It is to ask questions. To challenge assumptions. To demand measurable results. To distinguish between what would be nice to have and what taxpayers truly need. And, sometimes, to say no. Good leadership is not about cutting services simply for the sake of cutting. It is about making sure every dollar has a purpose and that taxpayers are receiving value for what they spend.So I will ask the question again: At what point do we say enough is enough and demand change? Here is how you can help!Every $25, $50, $100, or $250 contribution helps us reach another voter, put another sign in the ground, boost another digital ad and make the case for a different direction in Johnson County. And money alone will not win this election.We are in the final stages of this race, and volunteers are more important than ever. Knock doors. Make calls. Put up signs. Talk to your neighbors. I promise to fight to bring about positive change and fiscal sanity. Are you ready to join me? Karen Crnkovich Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair | | | | | | | | | PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION 6709 West 119th Street Ste. 224 Overland Park, KS 66209 * USA or |

# [Bank of America stock plunges 8% after $1.2B money-laundering fine and trading miss](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bank of America **[shares fell roughly 8.5%](https://substack.com/redirect/8d119db0-d5bc-4bd8-a2e4-9a4aa6e0d4da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday after third-quarter profit dropped 17% to $6.93 billion on a **[$1.2 billion Treasury anti-money-laundering penalty](https://substack.com/redirect/4b293a31-2ee7-4a34-9d41-440a96bd6c21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and weaker trading[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4f81b406-3e56-44e6-81f3-3ac677747b56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[that missed forecasts.](https://substack.com/redirect/4f81b406-3e56-44e6-81f3-3ac677747b56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trading results lag:** Fixed-income trading fell 17% to $2.55 billion and equities rose 10% to $2.51 billion, together missing StreetAccount estimates by about $750 million.
* **Adjusted profit light:** Excluding the penalty, earnings were $1.08 a share versus the $1.10 LSEG consensus on revenue of $30.12 billion.
* **Lending income higher:** Net interest income rose nearly 8% to about $16.5 billion on higher balances, slightly topping forecasts.
* **Analyst view harsh:** Wells Fargo's Mike Mayo called the capital-markets results "easily worst in class" for the quarter. At time of publishing the shares had rebounded slightly to down 6%.

# [Houthi missile slams Aramco Dhahran HQ as fire guts top floors](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A Houthi missile **[struck an administrative building](https://substack.com/redirect/6c156713-22e0-44a3-b691-45f7fdd78d74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters Tuesday night, causing a limited fire and extensive damage across multiple floors with no reported casualties.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Damage details emerge:** Sources said the fire started on the ninth floor of the south wing and spread between the sixth and tenth floors, **[with the top three floors severely affected.](https://substack.com/redirect/03b3bfa3-58ea-4500-b56f-f58d2bfe362e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Operations continue:** The complex's operations center stayed active, though some staff were asked to work from home and certain functions shifted elsewhere.
* **Broader escalation:** The strike followed repeated attacks on Riyadh's international airport and came as[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/cda4c4eb-234d-473c-a794-1c3dca13d93c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[several Saudi airports were closed](https://substack.com/redirect/cda4c4eb-234d-473c-a794-1c3dca13d93c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid intensified fighting.
* **Pipeline expansion plans:** Separate reporting said Riyadh aims to raise East-West Petroline capacity from 7 million to 10 million barrels per day within two to three years.

# [Saudi OpenAI engineer charged with bugging executive conference room](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal prosecutors **[charged a Saudi national](https://substack.com/redirect/c549a0e8-2dd9-4461-823c-0804f0b53878?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who worked as an OpenAI engineer with **[installing a concealed recording device](https://substack.com/redirect/6c6611c9-8a7e-4011-bfdc-10170e8dd5c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a San Francisco executive conference room used for confidential research and deal discussions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Device and discovery:** The encrypted device, wrapped in toilet paper and plugged into a USB port on the back of a television, was found September 30 after installation around September 28.
* **Second device found:** Security located a similar device in a bag left unattended by the employee on October 5 along with his wallet and ID.
* **Arrest and charges:** Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was arrested October 9 and faces a charge of intercepting oral communications that carries up to five years in prison.
* **Company response:** OpenAI said it used its models to identify the source, found no evidence of model weights, source code, or customer data being taken, and referred the matter to the FBI.

# [SpaceX caps Ukraine Starlink speed at 100 mph, drones lose connection](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX applied a **[100-mile-per-hour movement limit to certain Starlink terminals in Ukraine overnight,](https://substack.com/redirect/0277a6ab-43b5-4e24-abae-347d80ed530d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/0277a6ab-43b5-4e24-abae-347d80ed530d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)disrupting military drone operations as Kyiv continued strikes on Russian refineries **[despite U.S. calls to stop.](https://substack.com/redirect/813298c0-5826-4527-ae15-fb55c422231f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f3ab3542-16d6-40b6-b622-64733deed348?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Restriction confirmed:** Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said the limit applies to the StarShield military package and took effect without prior notice to Ukrainian forces.
* **Operational impact:** Units including the 7th Air Assault Corps reported canceled missions after connections dropped at higher speeds.
* **Policy context:** Starlink's acceptable-use policy prohibits remote control of aerial drones or military activity unless contractually permitted by SpaceX.
* **Timing noted:** The change came as Washington pressed Ukraine to halt refinery strikes and as Ukraine reported continued use of other communications for some long-range operations.

# [Major banks cut off MAGA sellers and conservative groups, OCC report confirms](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A **[regulator's report](https://substack.com/redirect/ad4379b1-9b3e-4e0b-b191-b73c9c78713c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** detailed how nine of the largest U.S. banks used reputation-risk policies between 2020 and 2025[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/53414022-daf3-491b-83d4-0b27dbc12e65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[to restrict services to customers and businesses across political lines.](https://substack.com/redirect/53414022-daf3-491b-83d4-0b27dbc12e65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/233d1307-51e5-4e42-814c-e463e38e34ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Examples cited:** The OCC highlighted a merchant selling Trump and MAGA merchandise whose account was closed, a public-education organization favoring Democratic candidates, and a firearms company seeking IPO assistance.
* **Banks reviewed:** JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo, and five others maintained policies limiting oil-and-gas, firearms, tobacco, digital-asset, and certain other activities.
* **Regulator statement:** Comptroller Jonathan Gould said the report provides "irrefutable evidence" that the largest banks denied, debanked, and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses.
* **Probe scope:** The review examined nearly 100,000 complaints and roughly 50,000 documents totaling about 420,000 pages.

Friends,

Here's a little secret most politicians won't admit: I don't love running for office.

When I arrived in the California State Assembly, everybody would ask, "Don't you just love it? Don't you just love being on the green carpet?”

**My answer?_No._

I will never love it.**

Because when you love something, you'll do anything to keep it. And I won’t do anything to stay in office.

Throughout my tenure, both in the State Assembly and as Secretary of State, I have been determined to use my position to do what's right. That means not compromising, even when it would help my electoral chances.

I’ve dedicated my life to protecting voting and civil rights. That mission matters more to me than winning any single election.

Now, as California’s Secretary of State, I oversee elections and ensure voting rights for all Californians.

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Hi Derek — if
your inbox looks anything like ours, it’s probably filled to the brim
with emails asking for a donation.

We’ll be upfront: Yes, we’re going to ask you for a grassroots donation
at the end of this message... but we don’t want it to be like every other
email in your inbox.

We’re not going to ask for $50, $25, or even $5. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17294?t=1001&akid=622%2E245147%2EaKPDcq ]Instead, we’re
asking you to chip in just one dollar (truly, just $1!) to reelect a
Democratic Governor here in the most competitive battleground state in
the country.

Here’s the thing about this election: Yes, the outcome of this race is
going to change Pennsylvania’s future for years down the line. But it’s
going to change our entire country’s future too.

In 2020, Pennsylvania led the charge to thwart Donald Trump’s scheme to
overturn the election. But that didn’t happen by accident. It happened
because Pennsylvania elected Democrats to statewide office, years
before.

But if our opponent wins on November 3rd? Republicans will control
every state-level office in Pennsylvania. And
Derek, they won’t hesitate for
a second to follow Trump’s marching orders — even if it means
overturning a free and fair election.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17294?t=1002&akid=622%2E245147%2EaKPDcq ]Here’s the good news: Your $1 will stop them. We’re up against
Trump’s entire roster of Mar-a-Lago megadonors. But if every person
reading this message chips in just a buck? We’ll win. It’s that simple.
Please, can we count on your donation of just $1?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17431?t=1003&akid=622%2E245147%2EaKPDcq ]Donate $1 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17296?t=1004&akid=622%2E245147%2EaKPDcq ]Donate More→

We’re truly grateful.

JoshShapiro.org

name: Jon Ossoff
subject: You deserve an explanation...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3086%2E5691347%2EVNCz6A)

Hi Peter —
[**I’m writing to ask, humbly, if you will chip in $5 to my reelection campaign ahead of our important final FEC fundraising deadline tonight.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261014-5-f&utm_campaign=em261014-5-f&amount=5&t=2&akid=3086%2E5691347%2EVNCz6A)
Here’s why this request is so important, especially today:
This FEC deadline is our _final deadline before Election Day._ Tonight marks the most important fundraising deadline we’ve faced so far in our campaign, and one of the most critical tests of the movement we’ve built in Georgia.
After the deadline, we’re legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the Federal Election Commission — and shortly after, those numbers will be made public.
Everyone from Donald Trump to my Republican opponent and their billionaire allies are going to look at our fundraising numbers closely. Very closely.
If they think we look weak, you can bet they’ll flood the airwaves with even more attack ads designed to distort my record.
We have to show everyone that our movement in Georgia is thriving and unstoppable — that we have what it takes to build the strongest voter outreach and mobilization program our state has ever seen. Because that’s what it’s going to take to win this race.
That’s why I’m personally asking:
[**Will you make a contribution to my campaign before our critical final FEC deadline tonight? Every donation counts. Each one sends a powerful message that people like you have my back.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261014-5-f&utm_campaign=em261014-5-f&t=3&akid=3086%2E5691347%2EVNCz6A)
**[DONATE](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261014-5-f&utm_campaign=em261014-5-f&t=4&akid=3086%2E5691347%2EVNCz6A)**
Thank you for everything.
Jon

**Vermonters Deserve Real Plans for a Stronger Path Forward**
Montpelier, Vt – Governor Phil Scott today released a new television ad highlighting his plans to make Vermont more affordable, strengthen the economy, and build a better future for Vermont families and communities.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/yVqW85dOW1R?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)

The 30-second spot, titled “A Stronger Path” builds on the Governor’s message that Vermont can make meaningful progress on its biggest challenges through practical solutions, fiscal responsibility, and more balance in the Legislature.

In the video, Governor Scott outlines his priorities for the next two years, including lowering taxes, making health insurance affordable, improving infrastructure, strengthening schools and small businesses, and helping communities thrive.

And he reinforces his commitment to protecting Vermonters from the chaos of Washington.

**“Vermonters deserve real plans, experienced leadership, and results,” Governor Scott said.

“We know what needs to be done to make Vermont more affordable, grow the economy, and create more opportunities for working families. I’ve got the experience, determination, and plans to do it – and with more legislators who will work with me, we’ll get the hard work done.”**

Governor Scott added, **“There’s more work to do, and I’m ready to do it. With our plans, and a balanced Legislature, we can put Vermont on a stronger path and set a good example for the country and our kids.”**

_**With your contribution TODAY, we can make sure this new ad is seen across the state, highlighting the Governor's REAL plans to get things doe for Vermont. **_

\- Team Scott

**MEMO:** October FEC Deadline **** **_NY-17 is one of only three districts nationwide that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican member of Congress._** Mike Lawler is beatable. This is a winnable district. But we are in the fight of our lives. All polls show we can win this as long as we reach voters. Mike Lawler has already massively outspent us on TV ads, and Donald Trump is spending more on this race than he is on any other House race nationwide. They’re spending so much money because they are afraid. Mike Lawler has beaten two politicians before. But he’s never beaten a patriot like Cait. And he’s never faced a campaign like this before! We’ve already knocked over 90,000 doors and made over 400,000 calls reaching voters and mobilizing an unstoppable field force. **_About Cait:_** Cait Conley is a proud fourth-generation Hudson Valley native from a blue collar family. After graduating from West Point, she spent 16 years as an active duty Army officer, deploying six times overseas to keep America safe. She’s spent her entire career protecting Americans and taking on tough fights. She has what it takes to beat Lawler and flip this district. **_Tonight:_** It is no exaggeration to say these might be the biggest 24 hours of our campaign. Tonight, Cait takes the stage for the last time to debate Mike Lawler. At the same time, midnight is our last FEC deadline. After, we’ll need to publicly report how much we’ve raised, and from how many donors. New York is the single most expensive place to run a political campaign—and Nate Silver has called NY-17 one of the three most likely seats to determine control of the House. So every pundit in the country is going to be watching us to see if we have what it takes to finish the job in November. **_Where you come in:_** Our campaign isn’t like Lawler’s—we’re powered by everyday people chipping in what they can afford, when they can afford it. **The bottom line: The only way we’ll be able to raise the funds to run a competitive campaign is with your help.**
